The gate accounts for EVERY file since d24c318 - an unrecognised vector FAILS rather than being silently skipped, which is what forced the mutable vector to be wired in rather than merely committed. REMAINING GAP: BOTH-ENDIANNESSES is still unmet - Connext on x86 emits little-endian only, so big-endian vectors must come from the XTypes worked examples, hand-derived and pinned to clause + page. 2026-07-25 (2nd vendor): mutabledata-fastdds.bin adds eProsima Fast DDS for the SAME sample. It is DECODE-verified, not byte-compared, because the two vendors DISAGREE on three fields of the XCDR1 parameter framing and both readings are defensible: Connext pads a parameter length to a multiple of 4 (4 for a 2-octet short, 12 for a 10-octet string) and sets FLAG_MUST_UNDERSTAND on the terminator (0x7F02); Fast DDS declares the exact ssize (2, 10) with a bare 0x3F02. Rules (24)/(25) say M.value.ssize - the Fast DDS reading; a PL_CDR list is also the RTPS ParameterList of RTPS 2.5 9.4.2.11 where lengths are 4-multiples - the Connext reading. NO ENCODER CAN BE BYTE-EXACT AGAINST BOTH, so ours matches Connext (the strict oracle) as a deliberate CHOICE, and this vector pins the half that must hold either way: that we DECODE the other vendor. Falsified by corrupting a member id. Both vendors send @mutable as PL_CDR, so NEITHER exercises PL_CDR2 and the XCDR2 length-code choice remains externally unpinned - a tested answer now, not an open unknown. BIG-ENDIAN, 2026-07-25: hand-derived BE byte vectors for MUTABLE in both encodings (mutable-xcdr2-bytes-be / mutable-xcdr1-bytes-be in gen-mutable), plus a BE/LE same-length assertion - endianness reorders octets within a field and never changes how many there are, so a length difference is an ALIGNMENT bug rather than a byte-order one and the two are easy to confuse when only one endianness is exercised. Falsified: byte-swapping the expected BE i64 turns it red. HONEST LIMIT, and it does NOT close the requirement: these octets are derived from the clause (EMHEADER1, parameter ids and lengths are UInt16/UInt32 in stream endianness per 7.4.3.4.2, so each is byte-reversed while the octet string and padding are not), NOT produced by an independent implementation. NO EXTERNAL BE ORACLE IS OBTAINABLE HERE: RTI Connext and Fast DDS both run little-endian on this hardware, neither exposes an endianness selector, and a library CDR buffer is not the wire (the to_cdr_buffer lesson, ADR 0061). WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE IT: a peer on a big-endian host, or a big-endian TRANSMIT path on our side (encapsulation-id-for returns only LE ids and %serialize-sample hardcodes :endianness :little, so we cannot currently emit BE at all) whose output a foreign decoder then verifies. The second is a contract change and wants an ADR.

Method: TX in the writer's offered representation — XCDR1-LE byte-exact + TX->RX round-trip (DDS-XTypes 1.3 §7.6.3.1.1; §7.6.3.1.2 Table 60)

Method: SHMEM-send self-guard: a signalled %shmem-send hard fault -> UDP fallback + counter + sender-error hook; the fault-vs-lane-full distinction (WP-SHMEM-SEND-SELF-GUARD, ADR 0013)
Notes: WP-SHMEM-SEND-SELF-GUARD DONE 2026-06-18 (ADR 0013 SHMEM-send-self-guard note; standard DDS, NOT R6). A SIGNALED %shmem-send hard fault (segment detached / pshared / bounds) is caught in %send-raw-buf (dds.disc), bumps disc-node-shmem-send-faults, fires *sender-emit-error-hook* (context :shmem-send-fault, via %note-shmem-send-fault, ignore-errors-guarded), and falls back to UDP exactly like a return-0 -> the datagram still delivers (a genuinely lost reliable sample repairs via HEARTBEAT/ACKNACK, RTPS 2.5 §8.4 / §8.4.1). The catch lives in dds.disc (not the dds.xport SHMEM :send lambda) so the counter + hook stay in scope with NO upward dds.xport->dds.disc dependency; the :send lambda stays unguarded so it can signal up. FAULT-VS-LANE-FULL: the handler-case fires ONLY on a SIGNAL; a benign lane-full (the SHMEM send RETURNS 0) takes the SILENT UDP fallback with NO counter bump / NO hook fire. Local send-error handling is implementation-defined (no RTPS clause); the UDP-fallback delivery is MORE conformant than a drop. Test affordance dds.xport.shmem:*debug-shmem-send-fault* (special, default NIL, exported) injects shmem-send-test-fault at the top of %shmem-send; NIL = byte-identical production, never wire-triggered (NFR-SEC-POSTURE). Method: Always-on CNSA-2.0 Data-At-Rest Encryption over the durability store (ADR 0021 cap.7): KEM-DEM envelope (ML-KEM-1024 -> HKDF-SHA384 DEK -> per-store AES-256-GCM, counter nonce, AAD-bound metadata, fail-closed), pluggable key-provider/KMS hook, all-secrets foreign/static, OpenSSL >= 3.5 native crypto (no hand-rolling, FR-SEC-2), bounds-checked + fuzzed open path, cross-DDS wire transparency

ENVELOPE: per-store ML-KEM-1024 (FIPS-203) encapsulate -> HKDF-SHA384 DEK (RFC 5869, info='dds-dare/dek/v1') -> AES-256-GCM (SP 800-38D) per record with a 96-bit COUNTER nonce; AAD = topic || writer-guid(16) || sn(8 LE) || kind(1) (authenticated cleartext so the inner store indexes/replays); on-store bytes = version(1) || nonce(12) || ciphertext || tag(16). NIST/IETF KATs (the conformance oracle, PUBLISHED sources, NEVER self-generated): AES-256-GCM vs NIST SP 800-38D Test Case 16 (run-dare-aes-gcm-kat-test); SHA-384 vs FIPS-180-4 + HKDF-SHA384 vs RFC 5869 (run-dare-sha384-hkdf-kat-test); ML-KEM-1024 vs C2SP/CCTV vectors (run-dare-ml-kem-kat-test). Envelope round-trip + AAD + tamper + wrong-key (run-dare-envelope-test); decorator seal/unseal byte-exact + tamper-drop + delegate (run-dare-encrypted-store-test, run-dare-encrypted-store-lifecycle-test). CRYPTO LIB: OpenSSL >= 3.5 (3.6.2 on this host) via HANDLE-BASED CFFI (cffi:foreign-symbol-pointer on an explicitly-resolved *libcrypto* handle — fixes a LibreSSL global-namespace collision that broke Clasp; impl-agnostic, NO reader conditionals), no primitive hand-rolled (FR-SEC-2; libsodium NOT used — lacks ML-KEM + SHA-384). FAIL-CLOSED everywhere: open-payload returns NIL (never plaintext) on short/wrong-version/auth-fail blob; get-range DROPS a failed record + fires *dare-error-hook*; OpenSSL<3.5 / ML-KEM-absent -> hard startup error (dare-available-p), NEVER a plaintext fallback. SECRET HANDLING (owner 'all secrets' directive, conformance): the ML-KEM private key, the shared secret, AND the DEK live in foreign-backed static-vectors (zeroized + freed via free-secret-octets at end-of-life); the DEK is BORN in a static-vector (never transits the heap); secret frees unwind-protect-guarded (throw-safe). KEY-PROVIDER: pluggable closure-vtable (the KMS hook) + default file provider (ML-KEM-1024 keypair, perms enforced 0600/0700 + checked at open, fail-CLOSED on loose OR unverifiable perms, internal decapsulate so the raw private key never leaves the provider); run-dare-key-provider-test. OPEN-PATH FUZZ (NFR-SEC-POSTURE; the operating contract §4): fuzz-dare-open-payload (pbt-test.lisp, 3000 iters) feeds open-payload adversarial sealed blobs (short/oversized/random/all-zero/tampered/wrong-AAD/strictly-truncated-valid + a genuinely-sealed blob under its true AAD) -> NIL or the CORRECT plaintext, NEVER an error/OOB/crash; a (safety 0) arm reaches the same verdict (the bounds guards are explicit manual checks, safety-independent); SKIPs cleanly if OpenSSL<3.5 (the KATs then carry crypto correctness). CROSS-DDS TRANSPARENCY (per-feature DoD, light by nature — DARE adds ZERO wire surface): in-process authoritative proof run-dare-service-transparency-test (a DARE-wrapped service delivers byte-correct retained samples to a same-stack late-joiner; SBCL + Clasp, Clasp first). LIVE foreign-peer confirmation (interop/durability-dare/, 2026-06-19, BOTH peers): a DARE-wrapped durability service delivered byte-correct samples to LIVE TL late-joiners — CONNEXT 7.3.1 received 352 (service retained 403), FAST DDS 3.6.1 received 152 (= 152 collected) — and both captures match the plain-store transient wire BYTE-FOR-BYTE (replay EntityId 0x00000102, firstAvailableSeqNumber=1 held on every HEARTBEAT, CDR_LE (0x0001) on all DATA, NACK->retransmit). NFR-MEM: make mem stays 0.0000 (DARE is control-plane, off the measured CDR hot path) -> no bench. CLASP DETERMINISM via the PAL (clasp#1793 avoided): DARE secret buffers alloc/free through the impl-agnostic dds.pal:alloc-static/free-static (NOT static-vectors:free-static-vector directly) -- on Clasp free-static recycles into a lock-guarded zero-on-reuse pool, never the buggy interior-pointer GC_FREE of clasp#1793 that corrupts the Boehm heap; on SBCL it truly frees (same workaround the hot-path static buffers already use). Notes: WP-DURABILITY-EPOCHS-MAC (ADR 0045 §7.2, 2026-07-07). Closes the last ADR-0045 §7 tamper-evidence residual: DIR/epochs.dat (the DARE per-epoch KEM-ciphertext table) was entry-CRC-only; the CRC is UNKEYED, so an offline disk adversary could flip a stored kem-ct AND recompute its per-entry CRC -> undetected -> wrong shared-secret -> wrong DEK -> fail-closed decrypt-failure (an availability brick / tamper-evidence gap); rollback + reorder likewise unauthenticated. FIX: a keyed HMAC over epochs.dat. k_epochs = HKDF-SHA384(ss, info=dds-dare/epochs/v1) is the THIRD sibling off the anchor shared secret (alongside the log-MAC key + k_meta) — it CANNOT derive from a per-epoch DEK (the DEKs ARE the contents of epochs.dat, circular), so %mint-logmac-anchor/%load-logmac-anchor derive+return all three keys from the same ss (freed on every path). Canonical signed image version||count||[%frame-epoch-entry]* over the entries SORTED BY EPOCH-ID ASCENDING (deterministic; reuses %frame-epoch-entry so each entry is byte-identical to on-disk), MAC'd HMAC-SHA-256(k_epochs, dds-dare/logmac/epochs/v1 || signed) (the same %hmac-labeled construction as the grandfather/tail anchors, a fresh label, NO new crypto) into a SEPARATE MUTABLE DIR/epochs.mac (signed||mac(32)||crc32(4), fsynced via the shared %write-anchor-file; %read-epochs-mac bounds-checks EVERY offset even at (safety 0)). SEAL at clean close (%seal-epochs-mac, right after the tail-anchor seal, before the keys free); VERIFY at open (%verify-epochs-mac, AFTER %load-epoch-deks' torn-tail truncate-recovery, guarded on k_epochs non-NIL) by PREFIX-CONTAINMENT, forward-tolerant: absent->CLEAN; .mac MAC mismatch->fail-closed; count<N->:truncated; first-N canonical image != stored signed->:diverged; a table with >=N whose first-N match->CLEAN (the extra is a forward 1-ahead crash-append; a strict whole-table-equality check would BRICK it and is REJECTED). NO invalidate-at-open (unlike §7.1): epochs.dat is append-only + never authorized-shrinks, so the only at-open divergence is the forward crash-append -> simpler than the tail anchor. Test-only *durability-debug-skip-epochs-seal* (mirrors *durability-debug-skip-tail-seal*, inert by default) exercises the no-false-reject path. 1 new test run-durability-epochs-mac-test (7 arms): (a) tamper-ct RED->GREEN headline [flip a kem-ct + recompute its per-entry CRC -> the unkeyed CRC path STILL accepts it (%load-epoch-table loads clean) but the keyed epochs.mac catches it :diverged fail-closed; non-vacuous clean control]; (b) rollback/truncation DETECTED :truncated + a forward-append CONTROL; (c) reorder DETECTED :diverged [swap the two kem-ct payloads + fix both per-entry CRCs -> the id<->ct binding differs from the sealed canonical image]; (d) epochs.mac-forge DETECTED [flip a byte in epochs.mac's own MAC + fix its CRC]; (e) cross-restart CLEAN; (f) 1-ahead crash-append CLEAN [the load-bearing no-false-reject]; (g) torn-tail CRC-recovery still verifies. Arms (a)-(d) assert the EXACT fail path via the condition report text (:diverged / :truncated / the epochs.mac self-MAC-mismatch wording) — botched byte-surgery cannot pass via a different error path. Residuals: the UNSEALED SUFFIX (epochs minted after the last clean close are unauthenticated until the next re-seal — the seal-at-close complement of forward-tolerance; damage bounded to fail-closed decrypt-failures of suffix-epoch records, never plaintext) + whole-file DELETION of epochs.dat/epochs.mac (the shared deletion residual, same class as anchor/tail deletion; sharpest form = laundering: delete epochs.mac + tamper + let the next clean close re-seal over the tampered table); torn-reseal recovery documented (:supersede in-place rewrite -> an OS crash mid-reseal leaves a torn epochs.mac that fail-louds at open until manually DELETED; absent -> clean, running-chain protection only); forward requirement recorded binding the epoch-table-retirement follow-on (retirement IS an authorized shrink -> that WP MUST rework the seal, e.g. invalidate-before-shrink + re-seal). Nonce-reuse confidentiality NOT at risk (each mint encapsulates a FRESH ciphertext even on id reuse) — integrity/availability + tamper-evidence-completeness, not confidentiality. Both impls 498 -> 499 passed (Clasp FIRST then SBCL; DARE available [OpenSSL 3.6.2] so all 7 arms EXECUTED, not skipped), IDENTICAL; gate-types (2577 defuns ftype-declared) + gate-hotpath (8 hot-path files clean; durability off the hot path) PASS; no new dependency (SBOM unchanged); no reader conditionals outside dds-pal.

Method: Autonomous background discovery (ADR 0056): create-participant :autonomous t spawns a per-participant announcer thread that periodically drives %spin-once (SPDP + SEDP announce + lease/liveliness/autopurge aging) so the application never calls spin (spin is a no-op in that mode). Lifecycle mirrors the S4 deadline monitor: spawn on create/enable, stop + condvar-signal-under-lock + JOIN in delete-participant BEFORE node teardown (no strand, no UAF). Cadence + announced leaseDuration come from the DISCOVERY_CONFIG vendor-extension participant QoS (discovery-announce-period default {1,0}; discovery-lease-duration default {100,0} = the RTPS 2.5 Table 9.18 PID_PARTICIPANT_LEASE_DURATION default, so the wire is unchanged at defaults), both CHANGEABLE and re-applied live by set_qos; a period >= the lease is INCONSISTENT_POLICY. Also fixed here: the SPDP leaseDuration Duration_t FRACTION (RTPS 2.5 §9.3.2.3) was written as 0 and ignored on receive, so a sub-second lease truncated to 0 = an instant false-prune of a live peer.

LIVE cross-vendor interop BOTH directions vs BOTH vendors, every leg with NO spin (interop/autodiscovery/README.md, 2026-07-11): Connext 7.3.1 writer -> our reader 252 samples; our writer -> Connext reader 27; Fast DDS writer -> our reader 131; our writer -> Fast DDS reader 29. Method: Type-gate false-REJECT fix (ADR 0057): a model parsed from a peer's LEGACY PID_TYPE_OBJECT_LB is assessed by ASSIGNABILITY with ALL bounds ignored — sequence, string, AND the XTypes §7.2.4.4.8 KEY sub-bound — and can NEVER be rejected on a bound. A legacy TypeObject is not a faithful encoding of the peer's declared type: rtiddsgen silently bounds an unbounded string at 255 (ADR 0009), so a stock Connext peer whose IDL says @key string color announces a 255-bounded KEY. The gate previously judged a remote READER under the §7.6.3.4.1 assumed DISALLOW_TYPE_COERCION (i.e. by struct EQUIVALENCE) and enforced the key sub-bound rule, both of which compare that invented bound — so it rejected a peer using the very same type, blocking EVERY DCPS DataWriter from matching EVERY stock vendor DataReader. New assignability-options ignore-key-bounds (default NIL = the spec rule; set ONLY by the legacy rung). The gate is not disarmed: extensibility, member count, ids, names, kinds, key FLAGS and must_understand still reject as before. Consequence recorded: against a legacy-only peer an explicit local DISALLOW_TYPE_COERCION cannot be honoured soundly and is downgraded (logged).

Method: The DDS 1.4 THREE-MASK sample selection (§2.2.2.5.3 / §2.2.2.5.2.7 / §2.2.2.5.8): sample_states + view_states + instance_states, closing the v1 sample-state-only deferral (ADR 0053 §2.4). Method: ADR 0058 — the ZC/SHMEM in-slot data_protection SecuredPayload overlay (ADR 0051) now serves the SIGN tier as well as ENCRYPT, so a SIGN-only wire-protected writer regains Zero-Copy instead of being gated off. %zc-overlay-eligible-p no longer demands key-material-encrypt-p; an AES256-GMAC EntityCrypto KM seals a GMAC SecuredPayload into the slot — the payload stays VISIBLE (as the SIGN tier leaves it visible on the wire) and is AUTHENTICATED by a common_mac the reader verifies fail-closed. The alternative ADR 0051 originally sketched (relax SIGN to RAW ZC, no overlay) is REJECTED: the RTPS signature covers only the 20-octet reference datagram, so a raw slot payload would be UNAUTHENTICATED — a co-resident process could tamper with the sample undetected, silently dropping the integrity guarantee the SIGN tier exists to provide. Gate relaxation only, NOT new crypto: encode-serialized-payload-into already implements both §9.5.3.3 sub-tiers and the reader's decode is gated on the overlay sentinel, not the tier. Carried with it: the send-side slot-capacity gate now uses the EXACT per-tier sealed length (new dds.security:secured-payload-length — ENCRYPT 44+N+pad4(N), SIGN 40+align4(N)) instead of a hardcoded ENCRYPT-only 44+len+3, so it can neither under-count (overflow) nor needlessly refuse a payload that would have fit. The single-shared-KM nonce invariant (ADR 0051 Forward Requirement) still governs: GMAC is AES-GCM with an empty plaintext and consumes the SAME iv-counter, so a second KM copy would reintroduce (key,nonce) reuse for SIGN exactly as for ENCRYPT. ALSO: ADR 0051 deferred follow-on 2 (-into-sap direct seal) is CLOSED as DECLINED on measurement.
Notes: Test zc-overlay-sign-tier (RED before / GREEN after): a SIGN-tier writer's overlay km is GMAC (not ENCRYPT) and IS overlay-eligible; the sealed SecuredPayload round-trips through the real §9.5.3.3 codec; a TAMPERED sealed slot is REJECTED fail-closed (the integrity the raw-ZC alternative would have silently lost); secured-payload-length predicts the seal EXACTLY for BOTH tiers. The pre-existing zc-shmem-secured-overlay test's GMAC assertion was FLIPPED deliberately (it pinned the old deferral). -into-sap DECLINED with evidence: the scratch->slot memcpy it would remove is only 2.6-4.5% of the overlay send cost (the AEAD pass dominates by ~25x) — bench/report/2026-07-11-zc-overlay-into-sap.md; not worth forking the one sealing primitive every data_protection tier depends on onto a second SAP-writing path, nor sealing into shared memory. Re-open if the memcpy share ever exceeds ~20%. 560/560 both impls, gate-hotpath + gate-types green; no wire-format change, no hot-path change for any non-overlay writer.

Method: ADR 0059 — discharge the four recorded FORWARD REQUIREMENTS (hazards unreachable today by a structural accident, with an instruction that a future WP must handle them). (1) %km-session-key-at two-slot publish (ADR 0038(a)/0039(d)): THE PREMISE WAS FALSE — the decode receiver is NOT single-threaded (start-node runs up to THREE receiver threads: unicast UDP + multicast UDP + SHMEM, all feeding %handle-datagram, able to decode from the SAME peer under the SAME participant KM) and session_id is read OFF THE WIRE, so a concurrent-different-session_id tear (KM advertising id S1 alongside key(S2) -> a later hit returns the WRONG key) was REACHABLE TODAY with no rekeying feature at all; fail-closed (a wrong key cannot forge a GCM tag -> the datagram drops) hence unnoticed, and safe only by the ACCIDENT that conformant peers use a fixed session_id. FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION: the discriminant + key are now ONE immutable session-cache object published by a SINGLE store (both the send-side cache and the receiver-specific origin-auth cache, whose discriminant is FOUR fields), so a reader sees the old pair or the new pair, never a mix. (2) ADR 0031 lim.1 decode-fail counters: DISCHARGED — each writer's counter table is STAMPED with the KM sender_key_id and RESET on change, so a future rotation cannot suppress samples encoded under the NEW key. (3) ADR 0043 reader-arming window: made FAIL-SAFE — the HEARTBEAT gate now requires the reader-side durability baseline to be ARMED as well as matched; a matched-but-unarmed HEARTBEAT is DROPPED + COUNTED (disc-node-hb-unarmed-drops, which MUST stay 0), so a WP that reopens the window pays one HEARTBEAT period of latency instead of shipping a silent DURABILITY violation. (4) ADR 0045 §7.2 epochs seal: cannot be discharged early (the seal deliberately cannot distinguish an authorized shrink from rollback tampering), so the :truncated ERROR now names its own obligation to the epoch-table-retirement WP.

Notes: Test km-session-cache-tear (new): hammers one KM from 4 threads x 6 interleaved DISTINCT session_ids and asserts (a) every lookup returns the key of the session_id it ASKED FOR and (b) every published cache object is SELF-CONSISTENT (its key is exactly what its own id derives) — for BOTH caches incl. the four-field origin-auth discriminant. Method: ADR 0060 — (1) DDS 1.4 §2.2.2.1.1.7 'a disabled entity does not communicate': a DataWriter/DataReader created DISABLED (its factory's ENTITY_FACTORY autoenable_created_entities is FALSE) is now WITHHELD from the wire — the disc node keeps a registered-but-not-yet-enabled EntityId set; announce-endpoints does not SEDP-announce them (plain AND secure SEDP — the filter runs before the discovery-protection split) and %match-remote-endpoint does not match them, so an inbound remote cannot bind to a disabled endpoint either; enable() calls enable-local-endpoint, which RELEASES it (the next announce advertises it, it matches, data flows). Registration stays EAGER (ADR 0052's reason holds: the engine EntityId is assigned at create); only VISIBILITY changed. Default autoenable path -> the table is empty -> announce/match sets are byte-identical. WHY IT WAS BROKEN: ADR 0052 §3 deferred true deferred-registration arguing 'discovery is spin-driven, so a disabled endpoint that is never spun never announces' — already thin (an app spinning for its OTHER endpoints announces the disabled one too) and KILLED OUTRIGHT by S7's autonomous announcer (ADR 0056): the participant now spins ITSELF. Measured before the fix: two autonomous participants each holding a DISABLED endpoint MATCHED anyway (matched=1 both sides). Lesson recorded in the ADR: a deferral justified by 'nothing currently exercises this path' is only as durable as the reason nothing exercises it. (2) ADR 0054's v1 non-trigger CLOSED: reader-suppress-sn (a permanently-undecodable secured SN, ADR 0031 lim.1) now raises SAMPLE_LOST — suppression stops the reader NACKing the SN, so no retransmit can EVER recover it; not counting it meant a real irrecoverable loss reached the application with NO status (SAMPLE_LOST.total_count stayed 0 while the sample simply never arrived, which is exactly what DDS 1.4 §2.2.4.1 defines SAMPLE_LOST for). Fired via the same hook + route fan-out as the irrecoverable-GAP path, OUTSIDE the node lock.
Notes: Test dcps-disabled-endpoint-silent (new, RED before): two AUTONOMOUS participants each holding a DISABLED endpoint do NOT match after 2.5 s of announcing (RED: matched=1 both sides), and enable() then RELEASES them — they match and a sample flows end-to-end (the fix WITHHOLDS, it does not strand). Test decode-fail-suppress (extended): the arm that trips suppression now also asserts SAMPLE_LOST fires on the matched DataReader (RED before: the loss was silent). ALSO CLOSED WITHOUT CODE, honestly: the ADR 0052 §3 node-scoped-pool deferral is BY DESIGN (the ZC/secured pools + per-node arenas are SHARED across a participant's N endpoints per ADR 0048, so deleting one of N must not tear down a pool a sibling still uses — bounded by the participant lifetime, not a leak, not a UAF), and the file backend's topics.map-loss cross-restart non-reclaim is benign + SQLite-immune. 562/562 both impls, gate-hotpath + gate-types green; no wire-format change, no hot-path change.

Method: ADR 0081 slice 3 — same-host detection against RTI Connext shared memory, by RTI's own published test (transport_shmem.h:89-96): attach read-only to the System V segment keyed 0x400000+RTPS-port and compare its shmemUUID against the 12 octets in the peer's advertised Locator_t. There is no locator-only way to decide co-location; RTI's header states the test requires reading the segment.
Notes: Segment layout MEASURED, not published — established by controlled variation (a documented Connext QoS property set to a distinctive value, then the segment diffed), so each offset is identified by a chosen value appearing where predicted: receive_buffer_size @0x58 (set 777216, read 777216), message_size_max @0x5c (set 20480, read 20480), received_message_count_max @0x60 (set 37, read 37). shmemUUID @0x24 PROVEN byte-identical to the same participant's SPDP-advertised locator address, measured simultaneously. Addressing CORRECTED from the slice-1 record: segment key is 0x400000+port (NOT 0x800000); semaphore 0x800000+port; mutex 0xB00000+port — confirmed by the header field order (transport_shmem.h:50-66 vs the :194-199 initialiser), by live ipcs, and by predicting the keys for six domains before starting a peer on each. NEW PAL surface sysv-shm-attach-readonly/-create/-detach/-destroy/-sap, one CFFI implementation serving SBCL and Clasp, no reader conditionals (gate-pal green); least-bytes IS the bounds check and the KERNEL enforces it (shmget returns EINVAL when the segment is shorter than requested), which is why no shmctl(IPC_STAT) wrapper exists — struct shmid_ds differs between Darwin and Linux. SHM_RDONLY/IPC_CREAT/IPC_EXCL/IPC_RMID read from sys/shm.h+sys/ipc.h on BOTH platforms, identical. Returns FOUR outcomes, not a boolean: (T NIL) same host; (NIL NIL) well-formed but another host (ordinary, NOT an error); (NIL :no-such-segment); (NIL :not-an-rti-shmem-segment); (NIL :unvalidated-shmem-protocol-version) — an RTI segment of a revision this layout was not measured against is REFUSED, never parsed (RTI names five revisions and specifies none). TEST run-rti-shmem-recognition-test builds its own synthetic segment (no Connext needed) and drives all five outcomes; FALSIFIED BOTH WAYS — deleting the majorVersion refusal makes an unmeasured revision report T (a confident wrong answer), and short-circuiting the UUID comparison makes a foreign host report T. LIVE-VALIDATED against a running Connext 7.3.1 shapes_pub on domain 0: T at its metatraffic port 7412 AND its user port 7413; wrong UUID at that same live port -> (NIL NIL); real UUID at a port with no segment -> (NIL :no-such-segment). 578/578 SBCL and Clasp; gate-build PASS both (clean cache, self-falsified), gate-types/gate-hotpath/gate-nocond(0)/gate-pal green. SCOPE LIMIT: measured on macOS/arm64 only, Connext 7.3.1, shmem protocol majorVersion 2 — Linux/CI is the oracle for anything platform-shaped and the SysV surface is exactly that; re-measure there. Read-only throughout: nothing writes to a Connext-owned segment.

Method: ADR 0081 slice 4 — read an RTI Connext receiver's embedded shared-memory transport properties and bound what may be written to it. RTI documents that a receiver's properties are embedded in its segment and that a SENDER verifies compatibility before use, so this is a prerequisite for slices 6-7.
Notes: rti-shmem-segment-properties returns segment-size + receive_buffer_size (0x58) + message_size_max (0x5c) + received_message_count_max (0x60); rti-shmem-datagram-fits-p bounds a datagram by message_size_max — the shared-memory analogue of the ADR 0079 emitted-datagram-size interop contract. EVERY LENGTH IS CORROBORATED BEFORE IT IS BELIEVED: the size the segment states about ITSELF is a number written by another process, so the segment is re-attached at that claimed size and the KERNEL decides (shmget refuses a request larger than the segment) — a segment overstating its extent is refused with :implausible-segment-properties instead of becoming a bound that later sizes a buffer. Remaining plausibility checks are PHYSICAL, never policy (a buffer cannot exceed the segment holding it, all fields non-zero), deliberately NOT an invented ceiling, because false-REJECT of a conformant peer is the worst failure class (OMG-conformance directive) and a peer may legitimately configure any message_size_max its segment accommodates. Header magic + majorVersion checks factored into %rti-shmem-header-status so the co-location test and the property reader can never diverge on whether a segment may be interpreted. TEST run-rti-shmem-properties-test builds its own synthetic segment (no Connext needed): exact read-back of all four fields; the fits/does-not-fit boundary at message_size_max and message_size_max+1; and three refusals — a segment CLAIMING twice its real extent, a receive_buffer_size beyond the segment, and a zero message_size_max. FALSIFIED: removing the kernel corroboration makes the overstating segment ACCEPTED, returning a properties struct carrying the lie (segment-size 8192 from a 4096-byte segment). LIVE-VALIDATED against a running Connext 7.3.1 shapes_pub on domain 0 ports 7412 AND 7413: segment=1115312 (matches ipcs segsz exactly), receive_buffer_size=1048576, message_size_max=65536, received_message_count_max=64 — all three EQUAL RTI's own published defaults (RECEIVE_BUFFER_SIZE_DEFAULT = message_size_max/4*count = 65536/4*64 = 1048576; MESSAGE_SIZE_MAX_DEFAULT 65536; RECEIVED_MESSAGE_COUNT_MAX_DEFAULT 64), and a 65536-octet datagram fits while 65537 does not. 579/579 SBCL and Clasp; gate-build PASS both (clean cache, self-falsified), gate-types/gate-hotpath/gate-nocond(0)/gate-pal green. Read-only throughout. SCOPE LIMIT: same as slice 3 — layout measured on macOS/arm64, Connext 7.3.1, majorVersion 2; no Connext exists on the Linux box so the layout leg cannot be re-measured there.

Method: ADR 0081 slice 7a — write a record into an RTI Connext receiver's shared-memory ring by the measured producer protocol, and wake it. First transmit into an RTI segment; foundation for full SHMEM interop transmit (7b live).
Notes: New System V SEMAPHORE PAL surface (sysv-sem-open/-create/-op/-setval/-getval/-destroy) + sysv-shm-attach-readwrite, one CFFI implementation for SBCL and Clasp; SETVAL/GETVAL command numbers differ per OS (Darwin 8/5, Linux 16/12 — the ONLY reader conditional; SEM_UNDO 0x1000 identical) — all read from sys/sem.h on both, SETVAL=8 cross-checked against a live Connext semctl via dtrace. rti-shmem-write-record follows the protocol measured in ADR 0081 §5.0 (traced directly): take the ring mutex with SEM_UNDO (so a crash cannot deadlock RTI's receiver), write the record at the producer cursor and advance it by align8(len), write the FULL producer control state (block A head + block B tail positions & counters + the (+datagram_length,0) descriptor entry — the write-set measured in ADR 0081 §5.0 by stopping the consumer), release, then raise the data flag with semctl SETVAL 1 (idempotent — the wake RTI uses, NOT semop(+1)). The mutex serialises writers; the consumer is lockless (matching our own reader). Bounded by message_size_max (:datagram-too-large) and the ring end. TEST run-rti-shmem-write-roundtrip-test builds a real RTI-shaped receiver (segment + mutex set resting 1 + data set resting 0) and proves write/read are inverses through real System V objects — TWO records so the advance is exercised, data flag confirmed raised to 1, mutex confirmed back to 1, oversized refused. FALSIFIED two ways: remove the SETVAL wake -> flag-raised assert fails; drop the cursor advance -> record B fails to read back. GATED on dds.pal:sysv-sem-setval-reliable-p (a runtime probe: create a private set, SETVAL 42, GETVAL, require 42): on Clasp/macOS-arm64 semctl's variadic value mispasses (ADR 0013, same NFR-PORT gap as shm_open) so SETVAL cannot wake the peer and the writer REFUSES with :setval-unavailable rather than landing an un-signalled record; the Clasp/macOS suite asserts that refusal. 582/582 SBCL and Clasp on macOS; 582/582 SBCL on Linux where SETVAL and SEM_UNDO were both confirmed to work (register varargs). gate-build PASS both impls (clean cache, self-falsified), gate-types/gate-hotpath/gate-nocond(0)/gate-pal green. SLICE 7b LIVE — ACCEPTED BY RTI. Against a throwaway rtiddsping pair with the publisher FROZEN (SIGSTOP, not killed: a killed publisher makes RTI's consumer unmatch it and stop consuming from that source, which invalidated three earlier runs), a record written by rti-shmem-write-record into a LIVE Connext 7.3.1 ring was DRAINED BY RTI'S OWN CONSUMER — consumer position 516->580 (+64, one record), consumer counter 8->9, all fields ending in sync at the new head, data semaphore cycling 0->1->0. Ring-level SHMEM transmit interoperability ACHIEVED. It took five live iterations, each naming one fault: (1) both block-A positions written equal (correct: idx4 = idx0+4); (2) descriptor slot off by one (the record taking the counter C->C+1 fills slot C-1); (3) the test itself killing the publisher; (4) the wake confirmed working (data-sem 0->1->0 proved the consumer woke and declined, isolating the fault to record CONTENT); (5) THE DESCRIPTOR SIGN — the producer writes +D (unconsumed) and the CONSUMER flips it to -D on drain, so writing -D made RTI read our fresh record as already-consumed and skip it. The diagnostic that cracked it was a producer-only control-region diff with the consumer SIGSTOPped (interop/connext/shmem-layout/ring-write-diff.sh): whatever a real producer write changes that ours does not is the missing field — it showed our write-set byte-identical except that sign. SLICE 7c — APPLICATION-LEVEL DELIVERY ACHIEVED (domain 79). RTI's rtiddsping subscriber COUNTED a sample this stack wrote into its shared-memory ring: issue-received 7 -> 8, the new line reading 'rtiddsping, issue received: 0000007' — a repeat of a payload counter already seen, which is the expected signature because only writerSN was patched and the payload was carried over verbatim. Ring level advanced in the same run (consumer A idx1 516->580, idx2/3 520->584, idx5/6 8->9; data semaphore 0->1->0). The publisher was FROZEN and PROVEN steady — the harness requires the counter to stand still for 2s before writing, so a freeze that did not take cannot read as success. Combined with the read path this stack now interoperates with RTI Connext over shared memory in BOTH directions up to application-level sample delivery. THE WHOLE OF 7c REDUCES TO ONE FACT: a verbatim replay can never carry a FRESH sequence number — everything still in the ring has by definition been delivered, so RTPS duplicate suppression (§8.4.13.2 best-effort accepts only SN > max received; §8.4.12 does not re-deliver an already-received change) drops it ABOVE the ring, which is why the ring-level milestone was real while the subscriber's counter never moved. Nothing about the segment layout was missing. Re-parsing the milestone record with this stack's own RTPS parser also CORRECTED the record: it WAS a user-data sample (writerId 0x80000003 is user-defined per RTPS 2.5 §9.3.1.2 — the class is the two most significant bits of entityKind — SN 2, 8-octet payload), not the participant-message it had been recorded as. TWO harness defects were found and fixed by live runs, each named: (1) the NEWEST record was excluded from selection because it has no following magic to bound it, so its submessage walk ran into the alignment padding and corroboration failed — selection then took the second-newest and injected the newest's own SN, a duplicate again; fixed by bounding it with head-minus-tail read off the ring (block A idx0 is the head, block B idx0 the tail, and the producer sets the tail to the pre-write head). (2) A suspected 4-octet placement bias was REFUTED by measurement rather than argued: the comparison had been made across two runs whose ring origins differ (offsets 808.. vs 816.., cursors 512 vs 516), which is not a comparison; the added placement check reports our record against the contiguous slot prev_offset+align8(prev_len) and measured delta +0 — rti-shmem-record-offset is correct. Harness: interop/connext/shmem-layout/{ring-records.lisp,live-userdata-retest.sh,live-write-retest.sh,ring-lib.sh}; the parse/patch path is falsified OFF-LINE (RTI_MODE=selftest, 13 checks, 3 of them falsifications: a one-octet-off patch and a wrong-byte-order patch must NOT read back, a builtin writerId must not classify as user data), and both the SN-offset constant and the padding guard were shown red. Read-write attach is used ONLY on the transmit path, bracketed by the ring mutex; everything else stays read-only.

Method: XCDR string encoding is UTF-8 (RFC 3629 §3), the encoding IDL/XTypes `string` requires — replacing a Latin-1 codec that refused every character above U+00FF and emitted single octets for U+0080..U+00FF that a conformant peer decodes as malformed. Topic and type names travel through the same codec in SPDP/SEDP, so the defect reached discovery, not only user payloads.
Artifact: src/dds-cdr/primitives.lisp (utf8-octet-length; %utf8-lead-length; %utf8-decode-at; cdr-put-string; cdr-get-string); src/dds-cdr/packages.lisp; src/dds-gen/dsl.lisp (serialized-size); src/dds-dcps/entities.lisp (write-sample boundary); src/dds-rtps/discovery.lisp; src/dds-types/typeobject-cdr.lisp; src/dds-types/typelookup.lisp; docs/plans/2026-07-23-utf8-string-codec.md; docs/wiki/cdr-and-memory.md
Notes: ENCODER asserted as EXACT OCTETS, never by round-trip — a round-trip through our own decoder passes even when both halves are wrong the same way: ASCII '(3 0 0 0 65 66 0)' unchanged; U+00E4 -> C3 A4; U+20AC -> E2 82 AC; U+1F600 -> F0 9F 98 80. ASCII is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the previous codec (UTF-8 is an ASCII superset), confirmed by corpus 11 vectors / 0 mismatches — that is what leaves every existing type untouched. DECODER REFUSES rather than repairs (returns (values the empty string :malformed-utf8)): bad lead octets, truncation, bad continuation octets, OVER-LONG forms, surrogates (U+D800..U+DFFF), and code points above U+10FFFF. Substituting U+FFFD was rejected by design — it hands the caller a string indistinguishable from one the peer sent. The primary value stays a STRING on the failure path because generated deserializers assign it into a slot declared `string` and NIL would be a type violation at (safety 0); the five callers that must not accept corrupt text check the status (discovery LEAVES a malformed topic/type name UNSET so the endpoint matches nothing rather than announcing the empty topic; TypeLookup drops the request; TypeObject rides its existing :unsupported channel). THREE DEFECTS EXPOSED, none about UTF-8: (1) write-sample's boundary caught EXACTLY ONE condition class while its comment claimed no condition may escape the public API — an over-long sample unwound buffer-overflow into the application, before this change, and removing the Latin-1 signaller would have left it catching nothing; now covers the serialization failure classes. (2) The generated serialized-size computed 4+(LENGTH s)+1, one octet per character, which UNDER-SIZES the buffer the sample is serialized into — a latent overflow, measured at estimate 13 vs 17 octets actually written. (3) A test used 'non-Latin-1 string' as its example of an UNENCODABLE sample; that premise is now false, so it was asserting a defect — re-anchored on an input that is still unencodable. FALSIFICATION CAUGHT A TEST PASSING FOR THE WRONG REASON: deleting the decoder's field-extent check left the suite GREEN because the truncated-sequence case was being caught by the continuation-octet check instead (the trailing NUL is not a valid continuation). Added a case only the extent check can catch — a prefix declaring 2 octets while a complete 3-octet sequence follows, so the third octet IS a valid continuation; without the bound the decoder returns U+20AC for octets the field never contained. The over-long falsification returns '/' for C0 AF, the filter bypass RFC 3629 §10 exists to prevent. 585/585 SBCL and Clasp; corpus 11/0; gate-build clean both impls (self-falsified), gate-nocond 0, gate-hotpath PASS. gate-mem UNCHANGED against a MEASURED baseline (1883.1/1878.4 baseline vs 1878.4/1885.1 with the change — overlapping ranges); an earlier '+27 B' reading had been taken against a REMEMBERED number, the exact error this gate's history warns about. OPEN, and not implied by the above: UTF-8 corpus vectors CANNOT be self-generated — scripts/capture-corpus.sh captures them from a LIVE RTI Connext writer and `make corpus` only verifies committed ones, so a vector we produced ourselves would prove nothing about interop. A live non-ASCII round trip through Connext and Fast DDS remains OWED.

FIX = a per-reader LEAF lock taken by all 12 reader entry points, which buys BOTH memory safety (no two threads inside a table at once) and atomicity of the compound read-modify-writes (get-or-create proxy, seen-test-then-mark dedup, read-compare-write last-sn). Per-impl synchronized tables were tried for the memory-safety half and REJECTED on measurement: with every entry point locked they are a redundant inner lock costing 4x more (+150 ns/sample vs +31 ns/sample). Cost of the shipped fix = +31 ns/sample, ~0.1%% of an end-to-end latency in tens of microseconds. VERIFIED on Linux with gencgc validating the whole heap on every GC (verify_gens=0): 603 tests green per run against a 5/10 corruption rate before. FALSIFIED not assumed: reader-concurrent-receivers (4 threads, 1 reader, same 500 SNs) is RED without the lock at 503/519/502 accepts for 500 SNs = observed DOUBLE DELIVERY violating RTPS 2.5 §8.3.5.4 exactly-once, and green with it. Supersedes the root diagnosis of ADR 0084 (withdrawn unimplemented) and corrects ADR 0078's (safety 0) premise: the repo has NO global optimize policy, so arena.lisp compiles at safety 1 where svref IS bounds-checked.

Method: raw-pointer rule enforced at the PAL socket boundary
Notes: ADR 0085: NFR-MEM's 'anything addressed by a raw pointer/SAP is foreign/static, never a plain heap array' was stated in prose at every SAP site and violated in production — dds.log:make-udp-syslog-sink passed each syslog line's freshly-consed UTF-8 octets straight to udp-send-to, and run-log-syslog-test handed recvfrom a 2048-byte GC-heap buffer to WRITE into. A moving GC can invalidate such an address underneath the syscall, so the kernel reads/writes whatever now occupies it (wrong bytes on the wire + heap contents disclosed to a remote peer on send; a datagram scribbled over live Lisp objects on receive). FIX: udp-send-to and udp-recv take the raw sendto/recvfrom path ONLY when dds.pal:static-vector-p holds and fall back to the GC-safe sb-bsd-sockets path otherwise — the same predicate sap-copy-out has always used. One predicate per datagram; the hot dataplane passes PAL-backed octet-buffer vecs so the raw path is unchanged. Found by auditing static-pointer's callers with a temporary tripwire (since removed — the guard is the durable fix).

Method: RX store-copy pool re-land + kill-switch
Notes: ADR 0078 re-landed under ADR 0085. The pool was reverted for heap corruption and re-diagnosed by ADR 0084 as a use-after-release RETENTION; both were wrong — a read cannot clobber an object header, and alloc-static memory sits in the glibc heap (measured 0x56BA22AC716F) entirely outside SBCL's dynamic space [0x1000000000,0x1040000000), so a write through a pooled buffer physically cannot reach a Lisp object. The pool was a TRIGGER only: it removes ~36 B/sample of GC-heap garbage, which shifts collection cadence and thread interleaving enough to fire the pre-existing receiver-thread race. Same-tree A/B with GC verification armed established causation (pool off 6/6 clean, pool on 5/10 corrupt) and the race fix cleared it. Retained from the investigation: the exactly-once release from a per-node rx-store-checkout set, the pool-release bounds guard (correct hardening for every pool, though never the corruptor at safety 1), and the new documented kill-switch dds.disc:*rx-store-pool-enabled* (T default; NIL = the pre-pool allocating copy, read per receive, no rebuild needed).

Method: TX key-hash scratch reuse under a CAS try-lock (make gate-mem before/after)
Notes: ADR 0087: the TX write path rebuilt its key-hash SCRATCH on every write - the RX drain stopped doing this at ADR 0075 but %instance-handle's own docstring recorded that 'every TX caller' still allocated fresh: a KEEP_LAST KEYED writer did make-octet-buffer + cursor + serialize + free-static per write (sized 112.0 -> 32.1 B/call isolated, n=200000, handles asserted byte-identical across arms). Fixed by reusing a per-writer cursor (%make-keyhash-scratch now the ONE definition shared with the reader's), guarded by a CAS TRY-LOCK rather than a lock because DDS 1.4 places no single-thread restriction on write() and two threads serializing keys through one buffer would interleave into a WRONG instance handle; a loser takes the pre-existing allocating path, byte-identical, never blocking. The 16-octet RESULT array is deliberately NOT reused: it is retained on THREE paths (threaded onto the CacheChange for KEEP_LAST per-instance eviction; used as a dw-instances equalp hash key; and, when the offered DEADLINE is finite, as the dw-deadline-timers key via %deadline-touch-writer -> %deadline-arm-instance), so recycling it would alias every change's handle and mutate live keys - the deadline path being the nastiest because it is CONDITIONAL, so a recycled array would look correct until someone configured a DEADLINE - silent mis-attribution, not a crash; closing that last ~32 B needs the ADR 0076 stable-handle indirection ported to the writer and is the recorded follow-on. Measured end-to-end on BOTH arches: arm64 1852.2 -> 1769.8 (-82.4), x86_64 1902.8 -> 1777.4 (-125.4, same-image A/B redefining %write-key-hash to its pre-0087 body); ceilings lowered 1910 -> 1800 and 1950 -> 1810.

Method: control-path proxy-key cache, write-once + verified (make gate-mem before/after)
Notes:
ADR 0088 (owner chose Option B on principle - 'I want this fixed by construction' - over the per-thread PAL scratch they had first authorised): the control-path GUID was built per datagram purely to index the ReaderProxy table. ADR 0062's blanket 'cannot become a shared scratch' is TOO STRONG - get-reader-proxy/%get-writer-proxy retain the key ONLY on creation (measured 9901 lookups : 1 create over 3000 samples). Fixed by (a) %retained-endpoint-key COPYING the key at the single point of retention, so a caller may pass a cached array - without it a reused buffer IS the live hash key, the next datagram mutates it in place, the proxy becomes unfindable and the writer's acked-base SILENTLY stops advancing; and (b) a bounded WRITE-ONCE per-writer key cache (writer-lookup-key) whose every hit is VERIFIED octet-for-octet (%guid-names-endpoint-p). SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION not by audit: entries are never mutated after publication so a concurrent receiver thread sees a whole valid GUID or nothing and the verify decides - a race can only MISS never return a wrong key, hence no lock and no audit obligation on future callers. arm64 1769.8 -> 1742.1 (-27.7). ⚠️ THE FIRST CUT WON NOTHING (+1.6 B): the miss-path builder was passed as a CLOSURE, which allocates on every call INCLUDING cache hits - swapping a 32-octet GUID for a closure; no correctness test could catch it (code right, cache hitting, all assertions green, optimisation simply absent) and only gate-mem exposed it. Two corrections forced: %source-guid's isolated 32.1 B/call over-reports the in-situ 19.9 B/call by ~1.6x (same class as ADR 0062's own ~3.5x correction - size in situ, treat per-site numbers as upper bounds); and %lane-drain's 393.6 B/sample is INCLUSIVE of on-datagram (the whole receive pipeline) so it is NOT an independent target - children-subtracted, the 817.8 B/sample receiver phase is the SUBMESSAGE HANDLERS led by %on-user-acknack (~240 -> ~212), then %handle-datagram own ~153, %on-user-heartbeat ~109, %on-user-data own ~66, dispatch-message own ~22. Falsified by run-proxy-key-retention-test, 5 assertions, the load-bearing one SEEN RED before being believed (disabling only the copy -> TEST FAILED [PROXY-KEY-RETAINED]); the rest pin the cache (hit is the same object, colliding slot with a different prefix rejected, different entity-id rejected, bounded under 64 distinct endpoints - a peer chooses how many readers it creates, so an unbounded cache would be remote-drivable).
Falsified by three assertions in run-keeplast-keyhash-threaded-test: tx-keyhash-not-aliased (captures the first handle BY REFERENCE, so pooling the result array makes it fail), tx-keyhash-fallback-identical, and tx-keyhash-lock-released (a leaked try-lock is invisible to correctness - handles stay right and the writer silently allocates forever after).

Method: relay dedup is O(1) and both its tables are capped
Notes: reader-dedup-accept-p is the exactly-once gate for relay-forwarded samples (PID_ORIGINAL_WRITER_INFO, RTPS 2.5 §8.3.5.4) and BOTH of its tables were driven by WIRE-SUPPLIED data with a resource-exhaustion hole. (1) CPU: the out-of-order set was an EQL hash capped by shedding the highest entry, found with a full loop-maximize over the table on EVERY call once at cap — at the shipped *max-gap-range*=65536 that is a 65536-key scan per sample, MEASURED 146401/142369/144440 ns/call, and a peer streaming SNs above the watermark drives it directly (one sender saturates a receiver thread). Replaced by a CIRCULAR BIT WINDOW over (lo, lo+window] indexed (mod sn window): test/set a bit and advance lo through the completed run, no scan and no shed. MEASURED 35.7/34.8/35.6 ns/call = ~4100x; the in-order path also improved ~1.6x (55.6 -> 34.5 ns) because it now touches no table at all, and the window is allocated LAZILY so in-order traffic never allocates it. Memory per origin at cap: 65536 hash entries -> a 65536-bit window = 8 KB. An SN beyond lo+window is ACCEPTED but not recorded — the same bounded residual the shed had (benign duplicate on re-arrival), never silent loss. (2) MEMORY: the origin table was keyed by the wire-supplied ORIGINAL_WRITER GUID with NO CAP, so any peer able to send a DATA could mint unbounded origins each with its own window. New *max-dedup-origins*=256 caps it; at the cap a NEW origin is refused and its samples are ACCEPTED UNTRACKED (duplicate risk, never a drop — a false reject is the worse failure) and tracked origins are NEVER evicted (evicting a watermark would risk double-delivering everything it had dedup(ed), per ADR 0024 §10.2). Refusals counted + readable via reader-dedup-origins-refused (reported, never printed). FALSIFIED: dedup-origin-cap goes RED with the cap removed; the pre-existing original-writer-dedup and dedup-cap tests pin the observable semantics (incl. the lo=4 -> lo=8 watermark path across a withheld gap SN and the shed entry re-admission) and stay green unchanged.

Method: unit + BYTE-EXACT vector + LIVE bidirectional Connext 7.3.1
Artifact: src/dds-gen/dsl.lisp; src/dds-cdr/primitives.lisp; dds-tests gen-test (gen-mutable); corpus/xcdr2/mutabledata-connext.bin; interop/connext/mutable/; interop/connext/mutable/ (mutable_pub + mutable_sub); scripts/gate-interop.sh legs 8/9
Notes: MUTABLE extensibility shipped (ADR 0086): define-dds-type accepts :mutable with per-member :id (@id, defaulting to declaration order, duplicates rejected at macroexpansion) and :must-understand (@must_understand). BOTH encodings emitted, selected at runtime by the codec mode, because a stock foreign reader may request either and XCDR2 framing under an XCDR1 encapsulation id would be silently wrong bytes: XCDR2 = XTypes 1.3 rules (21)-(22) DHEADER + EMHEADER1 per member; XCDR1 = rules (23)-(25) PL_CDR parameter list, each member ALIGN(4) + PUSH(ORIGIN=0), short form (id<PID_EXTENDED and ssize<=2^16) else long form via PID_EXTENDED 0x7F01 + eMemberHeader + llength, closed by PID_LIST_END 0x3F02. Table 60 ids PL_CDR2_LE 0x000b / PL_CDR_LE 0x0003, and %encap->codec now ACCEPTS them on RX (it had no arm at all, so the stack would have refused its own writer's samples). serialized-size is EXACT for both encodings and accounts for the framing (it had no mutable arm: every mutable write would have overflowed the payload buffer). deserialize-into likewise (it fell through to a positional read). Encoder emits LC 0-4, decoder handles 0-7; for LC>=5 the member extent is 4+width*NEXTINT because NEXTINT is the member's own leading COUNT and LC gives the element width - reading the spec's 'length is also NEXTINT' literally is 4 octets short per member and desynchronises the walk (ADR 0086 A1). Parameter id 1 is a MEMBER not a list terminator for a user type - the id-1 terminator is confined by Table 34 to Simple Discovery types, and accepting it truncates a default-numbered struct at its SECOND member (ADR 0086 A3). Test gen-mutable covers: framing bytes for both encodings hand-derived from the clause; round-trip x {xcdr1,xcdr2} x {LE,BE} with EXACT serialized-size; deserialize-into agreement; the compatibility property both directions (v2 sample with a reordered + added member read by a v1 reader skips the unknown id; a v1 sample read by a v2 reader keeps the absent member's default); must-understand DISCARD as a status not a condition (ADR 0064); the LC 0-7 extent table plus a hand-built LC=5 payload; engine round-trip through %serialize-sample / %deserialize-payload for both encapsulation ids; TypeObject carries the DECLARED ids not positions; and the hostile-wire rejections (member extent past the DHEADER, DHEADER past the buffer, PL_CDR list with no PID_LIST_END). EXIT GATE MET 2026-07-25: a live RTI Connext 7.3.1 MUTABLE payload is committed at corpus/xcdr2/mutabledata-connext.bin (72 octets) and our encoder reproduces it BYTE FOR BYTE under make corpus; the check is falsified (reverting the sentinel alone turns it red). THE VECTOR CORRECTED THREE THINGS no round-trip test could see, and settled a fourth question differently from how ADR 0086 posed it. (1) Connext sends @mutable as PL_CDR (XCDR1, encap 0x0003), NOT PL_CDR2 0x000b - so rules (23)-(25) are the framing that actually interoperates with it, and implementing both encodings rather than refusing XCDR1 is the only reason this works; the LC 4-vs-5/6 question does not arise on that wire at all and stays unpinned. (2) A parameter's declared length is rounded UP to a multiple of 4 with pad octets emitted (Connext declares 4 for a 2-octet short and 12 for a 10-octet string) - rules (24)/(25) say M.value.ssize, but a PL_CDR list IS the RTPS ParameterList of RTPS 2.5 9.4.2.11, and this repo's own dds.rtps.message:write-parameter had always done it for discovery. (3) The terminator is 0x7F02 = PID_LIST_END with FLAG_MUST_UNDERSTAND (Table 34 marks it must-understand), not the bare 0x3F02 rule (23)'s 'PID_SENTINEL' suggests; a decoder masks the flags off, so only an external encoder shows it. Capture tooling defect fixed alongside: corpus-capture read the buffer handed to %deliver-user-sample, which since the RX store-copy pool landed is a pooled SLOT rather than the payload (a 72-octet sample captured as 16396 octets of payload-plus-slack, looking entirely normal); both capture functions now disable the pool via SETF not LET, because the receive path runs on the receiver thread and a dynamic binding is thread-local. REMAINING GAP: no PL_CDR2 vector from any peer, so the XCDR2 length-code choice is spec-conformant but not externally pinned; and big-endian vectors still absent (Connext on x86 emits LE only). LIVE EXCHANGE ADDED 2026-07-25: make interop now gates MUTABLE BOTH DIRECTIONS vs Connext (legs 8/9) asserting every member VALUE, not a sample count - us->Connext 296 samples accepted by the strict oracle, Connext->us 30. That leg immediately found a defect the byte-exact vector structurally could NOT: a ONE-SIDED MATCH. Connext matched our writer while OUR type gate refused its reader, visible only as matched=0 plus one INCOMPATIBLE line. Both models agreed on extensibility, ids and kinds; the difference was one character in a member NAME - our TypeObject announced "t-ns" (from the Lisp slot) where the IDL declares "t_ns", and assignability matches members by NameHash. ROOT CAUSE was NOT mutable-specific: define-dds-type had no way to give a member a wire name differing from its Lisp slot, so NO type with an underscore in a member name could interoperate with a foreign peer, silently. Fixed by a :name member option (defaults to the downcased slot; duplicates rejected at macroexpansion) feeding the TypeObject NameHash and the content-filter field accessors; regression mutable-wire-name-* in gen-mutable. The gate now also dumps BOTH models on a reject when dds.dcps:*type-compat-log* is set - a bare INCOMPATIBLE named no failing condition. ADR 0086 A6.

Method: live Connext legs, BOTH directions (gate-interop legs 11/12)
Artifact: interop/connext/nokey/ (nokey_pub + nokey_sub, now runnable); scripts/gate-interop.sh Leg 11 comment; interop/connext/nokey/captures/
Notes: RESOLVED 2026-07-25, and NO_KEY was a RED HERRING. Both directions are now gated: us->Connext 74 samples (writer kind 0x03 matched), Connext->us 73 samples (reader kind 0x04). The outbound leg reported matched=0 and was briefly recorded here as an undiagnosed regression. Boundary instrumentation of the three decisions %match-remote-endpoint makes settled it in one run: the remote reader was discovered PERFECTLY - topic NoKeyTopic, type nokey-data, entity kind 0x04 all correct - and endpoint-match-p rejected it on (:DATA-REPRESENTATION) ALONE. A stock Connext DataReader generated from a plain IDL advertises XCDR1 ONLY; DATA_REPRESENTATION is an RxO policy; our XCDR2-default writer therefore SILENTLY does not match (matched=0, no error, no INCONSISTENT_TOPIC). run-nokey-publisher simply had no parameter to offer XCDR1 - the Shapes publisher has had one since WP-DATA-REPRESENTATION (ADR 0020) and its leg passes :xcdr1 for exactly this reason. Fixed by giving run-nokey-publisher :data-representation (default :xcdr2 per FR-CDR-4, the leg passes :xcdr1). SEPARATELY FIXED en route: the nokey peers could not START at all - the RTI libs carry an @loader_path install name that DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH cannot satisfy, so both binaries died with "Library not loaded". interop/connext/common/common.mk now symlinks the libs beside every peer as a post-link step, which is why these legs had sat built-but-ungated. LESSON: matched=0 has now been the symptom of THREE different causes in one session (a wire-name NameHash mismatch, a DATA_REPRESENTATION RxO mismatch, and an unrunnable peer); it names a symptom, never a cause, and instrumenting the match decisions costs one run and settles it.

Method: live Connext leg (gate-interop leg 25) + ours<->ours transition
Notes: FIXED 2026-07-25, same session it was found. LIVELINESS_CHANGED.alive_count was NEVER established when a reader matched a live writer: %reader-liveliness-changed had ONE caller, %on-disc-liveliness-changed, driven only by the discovery sweep on a TRANSITION - and the sweep already ASSUMES a freshly matched writer is alive (its prev defaults to T), so nothing ever told the DCPS status. The count sat at 0 while samples streamed in, and a later not-alive had nothing to decrement, which meant the ENTIRE status was inert. Fixed by recording ALIVE at match time and dropping it at unmatch, symmetric with the sweep assumption so the two cannot disagree; %reader-liveliness-changed floors at 0 so an unmatch after a not-alive cannot go negative. VERIFIED BOTH WAYS: ours<->ours now shows the FULL transition (alive 0 -> 1 -> 0 with not_alive=1 when the writer stops asserting and its lease expires), and against a live Connext MANUAL_BY_TOPIC writer alive_count reaches 1 with 12 samples. Gated as leg 25, asserting BOTH halves (samples prove the match was real, peak-alive>=1 proves the status was set) - it fails on the old code. 606/606 unaffected on both platforms. SECOND DEFECT, found and fixed immediately after: MANUAL_BY_TOPIC writers were IMMORTAL. %matched-writer-alive-p answered T unconditionally for that kind, on the correct observation that the ParticipantMessage protocol does not carry it (8.7.2.2.3 carries only AUTOMATIC and MANUAL_BY_PARTICIPANT) but the wrong conclusion - such a writer asserts by WRITING (8.4.13), so its DATA is the assertion and a reader CAN observe it directly. It is the one kind whose liveliness needs no protocol message at all, and it was the one kind that could never expire. Fixed by stamping each inbound sample against the effective (logical-origin) writer GUID and ageing that stamp against the offered lease; a writer with no sample yet stays alive (a freshly matched writer has not had a chance to assert, and calling it not-alive would fire a spurious NOT_ALIVE on every match), and stale stamps are reaped with liveliness-state so a re-matched writer cannot inherit evidence from its previous incarnation and the table cannot grow unbounded. Cost measured: gate-mem 1852.2 B/sample, NO regression (one PUTHASH of a fixnum per sample). Leg 25 now asserts BOTH halves - alive reaching 1 on match AND the NOT_ALIVE expiry - live against Connext.

Method: unit (status-registration-completeness, vendor-writer-status, writer-unacked-count) + falsification + a live 2-participant probe + make gate-mem before/after
Notes: ADR 0089: two VENDOR-EXTENSION DataWriter reliability statuses for RTI Connext parity - RELIABLE_WRITER_CACHE_CHANGED (bit 25) and RELIABLE_READER_ACTIVITY_CHANGED (bit 26). THE REUSABLE LESSON, worth more than the statuses: a status needs THREE registrations (*status-kind->bit*, *status-listener-invokers*, the on-<name> defgeneric) and EACH OMISSION FAILS SILENTLY IN A DIFFERENT WAY - no bit means its StatusCondition never triggers (only a WaitSet reveals it); no invoker means %notify-status FUNCALLS NIL on a receiver thread WHERE THE ERROR IS SWALLOWED, so the callback never arrives while every other path keeps working. The first cut registered one of the three, compiled, passed the suite, and fired ZERO callbacks on a live exchange. The registration itself is now asserted by run-status-registration-completeness-test, which walks both maps and requires all three for every status - exempting only DATA_AVAILABLE and DATA_ON_READERS, which are LEVEL-based and bypass %notify-status entirely. That test found, on its first run, TWO DEFECTS SHIPPED SINCE ADR 0080: UNADDRESSABLE_PEER was absent from *status-kind->bit* AND on-unaddressable-peer NEVER EXISTED, so its docstring had promised bitmask+StatusCondition+listener+snapshot while only two of the four worked. DESIGN: the cache status is EDGE-triggered AND EPISODE-GATED (a Schmitt trigger) - the high watermark OPENS a backpressure episode, the low watermark or a drain to empty CLOSES it, and the low/empty transitions fire only inside an open episode. Edge-triggering alone is insufficient because the window oscillates 0<->1 in ordinary traffic, so its crossings are still per-sample. FULL is deliberately NOT episode-gated: reaching RESOURCE_LIMITS max_samples is an absolute condition. THE WATERMARKS DEFAULT TO DISABLED, a deliberate divergence from Connext's documented {0, 1}: there the pair primarily drives an INTERNAL mode (the switch to fast_heartbeat_period) and the status change costs two counter increments, whereas here it drives an APPLICATION CALLBACK, and at {0, 1} an exchange with one sample in flight crosses high on every write and low on every ack - measured at +763 B/sample, but the byte count is not the argument: a status whose purpose is to announce backpressure must be SILENT when there is none. Disabled it still reports the FULL transition and still tracks its LEVELS (unacked count, peak, replaced-unacked), which is what makes a silent default honest rather than inert. THE UNACKED COUNT IS THE SEND WINDOW, NOT THE CACHE OCCUPANCY: the first cut passed hc-change-count, which coincides for a VOLATILE writer that has just purged - which is exactly why a live probe looked correct - and diverges for a TRANSIENT_LOCAL writer, which RETAINS its acked history for late-joiners so its stored count is the whole history forever while its true unacked count may be zero; it would have claimed unbounded backpressure on a perfectly healthy writer. writer-unacked-count is last-SN minus acked-watermark plus 1, clamped at 0, O(1), with the watermark now recorded by writer-purge-acked BEFORE its durability gate so it stays true for the writer that never purges. WITHDRAWN rather than shipped under a Connext name with different firing rules: on_sample_removed (Connext fires it ONLY for cookie / Zero-Copy-FlatData samples and hands back a DDS_Cookie_t for buffer reclaim; ours fired on every purge, and of its three documented reasons only :acked was ever fired - :replaced and :dropped were DEAD. :replaced now lives where RTI puts it, in replaced-unacked-sample-count; :dropped is already write()'s return code; the genuine cookie callback needs a writer-loan reclaim path ADR 0042's loan does not have. StatusKind bit 27 is left RESERVED, not recycled) and on_destination_unreachable (it DOES NOT EXIST in the Connext 7.3 DataWriterListener - it had been listed from recollection; Connext's real answer is the internal locator reachability ping, which stops using the locator rather than notifying anyone). on_instance_replaced is NOT wired: it needs an instance_replacement QoS and a writer-side eviction path we do not have (we REJECT at max_instances), so wiring a callback that can never fire would be the inert-status trap again. FALSIFIED, every assertion seen RED before being believed: level-triggered instead of edge-triggered -> :vwc-edge-high-once; episode gate removed -> :vwc-quiet-by-default; hc-change-count substituted -> :wuc-transient-local; invoker entry removed -> :status-reg-invoker; generic function removed -> :status-reg-generic. LIVE PROBE (2 participants, 40 reliable samples, a distinct domain per arm): with watermarks {2, 10} the cache callback fires exactly 2x (one high crossing, one low) with peak 28, and reader-activity 1x with active_count=1; at the DEFAULT QoS the cache callback fires 0x while still tracking peak=40. The first cut produced 12 callbacks for the same 40 samples.

Method: same-image A/B attribution + make gate-mem before/after
Notes: ADR 0089 §7: the vendor statuses put a notification on the per-sample WRITE path, so gate-mem governs. It caught +763 B/sample and same-image A/B attribution (never a profile - sb-sprof :alloc ranks EVENTS, not bytes) found THREE independent causes, only one of them obvious. (1) RTI's {0, 1} watermark defaults, ~530 B/sample: two real events per sample - a SEMANTIC defect that merely presented as bytes, fixed by the episode gate and a disabled default. (2) 123.5 B/sample from FOUR EDGE FLAGS setq'd under the status lock and then read by the notification closure: to SBCL those are four MUTABLE CLOSED-OVER VARIABLES and it heap-allocates A VALUE CELL FOR EACH, on every call, whether or not any edge was crossed. Fixed by returning them as bits of ONE IMMUTABLY-BOUND FIXNUM (+wc-edge-*+), which the closure copies. (3) 76.4 B/sample from %notify-reader-activity building its apply-fn CLOSURE unconditionally - %notify-status takes a closure and it was constructed on every inbound ACKNACK before anything had been tested; fixed with an allocation-free membership guard, since in steady state the answer is always 'this reader was already active'. (4) 43.7 B/sample from %participant-writer-by-entity-id, which went through %participant-writers - that APPENDs a fresh list of every writer in the participant per call, fine for its match-time callers but not once a writer is resolved per write and per ACKNACK; rewritten to walk the containment tree directly, allocation-free, and every other caller benefits. CAUSES 2 AND 3 ARE ADR 0088'S DEFECT AGAIN in two new disguises - a closure allocates on every call, including the calls where nothing happens - which cost ADR 0088 its entire first-cut win. The generalisable rule: ON A PER-SAMPLE PATH THE GUARD GOES OUTSIDE THE NOTIFICATION, NEVER INSIDE IT, because the argument to the notification IS the allocation. A fourth hypothesis - that bordeaux-threads:with-lock-held conses per acquisition - was MEASURED AND DISPROVED (0.00 bytes over 2000000 acquisitions) before any design was built on it. AS SHIPPED the whole slice costs 0.0 B/sample: same-image A/B on arm64, whole slice on vs neutralised, 1738.6 / 1738.6; gate-mem on the final tree reads 1740.4 against the ceiling of 1775 (main was 1742.1, so neutral; an intermediate 1738.2 and the final 1740.4 differ by 2.2 B, inside the ~3 B session spread bench/mem-ceiling.txt documents at 60000 samples - which is why the A/B, not the absolute reading, is the claim). THE CEILING IS NOT LOWERED - no win is claimed.

Method: byte-exact decode of CAPTURED RTI submessages (make corpus, falsified) + adversarial parse test (make test app-ack-hostile, falsified)

CHECKED BY EQUALITY, NOT BY RANK, and that is the safety-critical decision. Every other ordered policy has a safe direction where a stronger offer satisfies a weaker request; this one has NONE, because the two mismatches fail in OPPOSITE ways and NEITHER ANNOUNCES ITSELF: a :PROTOCOL writer matched to an APPLICATION reader purges on protocol acks alone, so the reader believes it holds an end-to-end guarantee it does not - SILENT DATA LOSS; an APPLICATION writer matched to a :PROTOCOL reader waits for acknowledgments that reader never sends, so its history grows until RESOURCE_LIMITS blocks or rejects - SILENT STALL. OWNERSHIP is equality-checked for the same structural reason. Two DIFFERENT application kinds also fail to match: when a sample becomes acknowledged is exactly what they disagree about. THE GOVERNING PRINCIPLE IS INVERTED FROM THE REST OF THE STACK - a FALSE ACK is worse than no ack, because a writer that believes a sample acknowledged may PURGE it and report success, so an under-report is a delay and an over-report is silent data loss. Every decision follows from that. ONLY ACCESSED SAMPLES ARE ACKNOWLEDGEABLE: both calls act on what the application has read or taken, never on what the reader merely HOLDS - acknowledging the cache would acknowledge exactly the samples this feature exists to keep a writer from purging. A sequence number the application never accessed is REFUSED with PRECONDITION_NOT_MET rather than acknowledged on faith, which also covers a stale, fabricated or cross-reader SampleInfo. SampleInfo.publication_handle is now populated on every delivery path, because a sample is identified by (writer GUID, sequence number) and a sequence number is unique only within one writer (RTPS 2.5 §8.3.5.4); it is ALIASED, not copied - 0 B/sample where a copy-seq would cost ~32 - and that places a CONSTRAINT ON ADR 0088: a memoised invariant GUID (its Option B) keeps this safe, a shared mutable scratch (its Option A) would rewrite a handle the application is already holding, which is application-visible rather than internal. THE STATE MACHINE IS BYTE-VERIFIED AGAINST RTI, not merely unit-tested: make corpus now drives acknowledge(SN 1) then acknowledge(SN 2) through the real API and requires the emitted octets to be IDENTICAL to the two captured Connext APP_ACKs. That is the slice-A2 round-trip lesson applied ONE LEVEL UP - A2 re-derived the LAYOUT from a decode, this re-derives the CONTENT from the API, and it is the only available oracle for a behaviour with no specification. It passed on its first run, reproducing the cumulative model exactly: a coalesced run of previously-reported sequence numbers plus the newly acknowledged one as a SEPARATE interval, never merged, with the count starting at 1. THE APP_ACK IS UNICAST TO THE ACKNOWLEDGED WRITER'S PARTICIPANT ALONE, AND THAT IS A SAFETY PROPERTY, NOT AN OPTIMISATION: a reader's ACKNACK is fanned out to every matched peer harmlessly because it is keyed by a SequenceNumberSet a foreign writer will not recognise, but an APP_ACK names a writerId and two writers in different participants routinely share an EntityId - fanned out it would tell a same-EntityId writer elsewhere that ITS samples were acknowledged by an application that never saw them. The live test asserts the NEGATIVE with a decoy participant holding a same-topic writer that receives ZERO. Emission is under OUR VendorId, never RTI's: claiming RTI's would make every other submessage in the datagram interpretable under RTI's rules and would be a lie about who sent it. Inbound 0x1c/0x1d are RECOGNISED AND COUNTED under a VendorId that gives them this meaning (RTI's, or ours for what we emit) so the ours-to-ours test can prove the datagram landed; recognised is NOT processed - the writer-side APPLICATION watermark, on-application-acknowledgment and APP_ACK_CONF are slice A3c. Notes: ADR 0090 slice A3c, the WRITER side - and the slice that makes the whole feature real. THE APPLICATION WATERMARK: a SECOND watermark on every ReaderProxy beside ADR 0089's acked-base, with the HistoryCache purge taking the MINIMUM of the two, so a fully PROTOCOL-acknowledged sample is retained until the subscribing application says it processed it. Without it the reader would emit APP_ACKs, the writer would report an end-to-end guarantee, and it would purge on protocol acks regardless - a writer reporting a guarantee it is not honouring, which is precisely the silent data loss ADR 0090 section 4 refuses to match on. THE MIN, NOT THE APPLICATION WATERMARK ALONE: the two are independent by design (section 7 Q1 - a sample can be protocol-acked and not yet app-acked, never the reverse) and min() is correct under either ordering, so nothing depends on an invariant a remote peer could violate. Gated on the writer's OWN advertised QoS (%local-writer-app-ack-p, resolved exactly as %local-writer-durability is), so the :PROTOCOL default is byte-identical and the second watermark, though present on every proxy, is consulted nowhere else. ⚠️ ONLY THE CONTIGUOUS PREFIX ADVANCES IT, AND THAT IS THE SAFETY PROPERTY. An APP_ACK may name disjoint ranges because the peer application is free to acknowledge out of order; a watermark means 'everything below this', so taking the highest named sequence number would declare every hole beneath it acknowledged and purge samples nobody processed - A FALSE ACK MANUFACTURED BY THE WRITER rather than by the reader. A gap stops the advance, the samples above it stay retained, and a later cumulative APP_ACK (which is what the capture shows RTI sending) closes the hole and releases the run in one step. MONOTONIC: a stale, duplicated or reordered APP_ACK can never retreat the watermark - un-acknowledging merely stalls, but re-acknowledging something already released is unrecoverable. THE ACKNACK PURGE SITE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: an ACKNACK is what normally frees history, so gating only the APP_ACK-driven purge would have left the watermark decorative. APP_ACK_CONF is emitted back to the acknowledging reader alone, echoing the count; inbound APP_ACK_CONF is COUNTED ONLY, because the reader re-reports cumulatively and nothing on it depends on receiving one. on-application-acknowledgment + application-acknowledgment-status at StatusKind BIT 28 (27 stays RESERVED - recycling it would silently change the meaning of any persisted status mask), with all three registrations; NOT edge-triggered and NOT episode-gated unlike ADR 0089's cache status, because an application acknowledgment is an EVENT the peer chose to send rather than a level that moves twice per sample, and suppressing any of them would hide the thing the callback exists to report. app-unacked-sample-count is DELIBERATELY DISTINCT from the ADR 0089 unacked-sample-count: the protocol window can be EMPTY while the application window is full, so a writer watching only the older number believes it has no backlog while its history grows. RTI's DDS_AcknowledgmentInfo fields response_data / valid_response_data are ABSENT ON PURPOSE - nothing emits or parses response data yet, so they would be permanently NIL under names that promise otherwise (the ADR 0089 section 5 inert-field trap). T10 GATED like ACKNACK: a forged plain APP_ACK would advance an application watermark and let the writer purge samples no application processed - the same permanent-data-loss shape, and worse here because the loss is silent by construction. The intervals are collected BEFORE anything is applied, because parse-app-ack-body is a visitor that may still reject the body after visiting some of them; applying as it visits would accept part of a message we then discard. ⭐ A FOURTH SILENT FAILURE MODE IN THE STATUS MACHINERY, FOUND HERE: %notify-status's apply-fn contract is (values CHANGED-P SNAPSHOT RESET-THUNK), and the first cut returned the snapshot ALONE - so it became the CHANGED-P value, the notification proceeded, and THE LISTENER FIRED CARRYING A NULL STATUS. All three ADR 0089 registrations were present and the completeness test passed, because it checks that the registrations exist, not that the payload arrives. What caught it was asserting on the status CONTENT: ':aae-listener-fired' passed while ':aae-listener-names-reader' failed. GENERALISE: a test that only asks whether a callback fired cannot distinguish a working notification from an empty one.
