Notes: ADR 0090 slice A4, the acknowledgment watchdog. OWNER DIRECTIVE, VERBATIM: 'We never must allow for a writer stalling - NEVER.' A3c made a writer retain until the subscribing application confirms; A4 makes that retention impossible to hide. THE CONDITION IS OTHERWISE INVISIBLE: a reader can match, receive and TAKE every sample and simply never acknowledge - its RTPS layer keeps ACKNACKing, so RELIABLE_READER_ACTIVITY_CHANGED still reports it ACTIVE and PUBLICATION_MATCHED still reports it matched. Nothing in DDS distinguishes 'processing slowly' from 'stopped processing', and the writer's history grows until RESOURCE_LIMITS, at which point write() fails for a reason nobody can see. ACKNOWLEDGMENT_DEADLINE is a DataWriter-scoped vendor duration, FINITE BY DEFAULT AT 60 s - a deliberate inversion of the ADR 0089 watermarks, which default to DISABLED on the principle that a backpressure status must be silent when there is none; here SILENCE IS THE DEFECT, so unbounded retention must be opted into with +duration-infinite+. APPLICATION_ACKNOWLEDGMENT_OVERDUE sits at StatusKind BIT 29 (27 reserved, 28 is the arrival status) with all three registrations, and is DISTINCT from bit 28 on purpose: folding 'an acknowledgment arrived' and 'none arrived' into one callback would make a listener inspect fields to tell progress from no-progress, the familiar-name-different-meaning trap of ADR 0089 section 5. ⚠️ IT REPORTS AND NEVER PURGES - releasing the samples on expiry would discard data no application processed, the false ack this ADR forbids outright; asserted by :aao-not-purged rather than merely stated. THE PAYLOAD IS THE POINT: the status names the LAGGARD reader (writer-app-laggard: the matched reader whose application watermark is lowest), the OLDEST unconfirmed sequence number, and the backlog - a bare count says there is a problem, a GUID and a sequence number say WHERE it is and HOW FAR BACK it reaches. An inert status is what ADR 0089 was written against. NO NEW THREAD: it rides the existing per-participant deadline monitor as a THIRD timer kind (:app-ack, keyed by a sentinel keyword that cannot collide with a 16-octet instance handle in that equalp table), armed on write and disarmed when the backlog drains; a :PROTOCOL writer arms nothing and pays one keyword comparison on the write path. ONE NEW PULL-SHAPED ACCESSOR, node-writer-app-unacked, and the direction is the point: every other engine-to-DCPS report in this stack is PUSHED from an inbound event that carries its state, but this fires because NOTHING ARRIVED, so no event can carry anything and dds.dcps - which must never resolve an rtps-writer - needs somewhere to ask. Keeping that pull explicit and singular is what stops the layer boundary eroding. A BACKLOG OF ZERO FIRES NOTHING (a drain racing an expiry is ordinary; 'overdue: 0 samples' would be a false alarm on a healthy writer). WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, measured in ADR 0090 section 3.3: it cannot stop a FOREIGN writer from retaining - RTI does not refuse to match a reader that cannot acknowledge, and DDS matching is per-side, so a local refusal cannot stop a peer from matching us. This protects OUR writer and makes our own refusals visible; the rest is outside our reach and is documented rather than papered over. FALSIFIED, both seen RED: setting the deadline INFINITE turns :aao-fired red (the explicit opt-out still works); purging on expiry turns :aao-not-purged red.

Notes: ADR 0091: stop-node hung FOREVER, intermittently - observed as 61 minutes elapsed for 15 seconds of CPU, blocked not spinning, with the whole suite reporting nothing. ROOT CAUSE captured live: a UDP receiver parked inside recvfrom(2) when stop-node released its file descriptor (#<INET-SOCKET fd: -1> still inside UDP-RECV) while the main thread sat in %CONDITION-WAIT on that thread's join waitqueue. THREE WAKEUP MECHANISMS ALL FAIL: close(2) does not unblock a parked recvfrom on Linux (already known - that is why udp-close shuts down first); shutdown(2) FAILS ENOTCONN on an UNCONNECTED UDP socket on macOS/BSD and wakes nothing, silently, because udp-close wraps it in ignore-errors; and SO_RCVTIMEO rescues a FRESHLY OPENED socket (measured: returns in 0.256 s) but NOT one already parked when the fd is released (measured: still parked minutes later). ⚠️ THIS CORRECTS A FALSE CLAIM IN udp-close's OWN DOCSTRING, which said the receiver exits when the socket is closed, TRUE ON DARWIN and FALSE ON LINUX. Darwin is RACY, not correct - and that sentence cost an investigation, because it contradicted the correct hypothesis (macOS shutdown/ENOTCONN) and the hypothesis was abandoned on its authority. A DOCSTRING IS A CLAIM, NOT EVIDENCE, exactly as a memory note is. THE DECISION: teardown must not depend on waking a parked receiver AT ALL. Three layers - (1) flag -> join -> close, replacing close -> join: stop-node sets disc-node-rx-stopping FIRST and each receiver loop tests it at the top of every iteration, so it leaves WHILE ITS FD IS STILL VALID and the unreachable state is never entered rather than merely survived - THIS IS THE FIX; (2) SO_RCVTIMEO on every UDP socket (udp-open -> udp-set-receive-timeout, DELEGATING to the existing tcp-set-recv-timeout so struct timeval is encoded once, not twice) bounding how long a parked receiver takes to NOTICE the flag at 250 ms, costing 4 idle wakeups/second per receiver thread off the data path; (3) join-bounded (5 s) as a backstop that should now never fire. ⚠️ A TIMED-OUT JOIN IS NOT SUCCESS: the joins guarantee no receiver is still writing into a buffer stop-node is about to free, so on :TIMEOUT the node is marked teardown-leaked, THE FREES ARE SKIPPED and stuck-receiver-teardowns is incremented - a bounded leak beats a use-after-free on a live thread, the same ranking the Zero-Copy refcount path already applies. That counter MUST STAY 0. REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: connect() the socket to itself so shutdown works (makes correctness depend on a SECOND per-OS behaviour, the very class of bug being fixed); a self-wakeup datagram (needs the stop flag anyway to close the re-park race, so it is the same design plus a packet); bounded join ALONE (leaves the receiver genuinely stuck ~40% of the time and leaking on every occurrence - contains the symptom, does not remove it). STAGED MEASUREMENT over 25 iterations of run-durability-supervisor-test, whose healthy iteration is 0.3 s: BEFORE it hung at iteration 3 every time; receive-timeout + bounded join alone gave worst 5.29 s with 10/25 hitting the backstop; adding the reorder gave worst 1.40 s with 0/25. FALSIFIED: remove the rx-stopping signal AND unbound the join => HANGS AT ITERATION 0. THE TOOL MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE FIX: an all-thread backtrace watchdog that fires on LACK OF PROGRESS (never on elapsed time, which cries hang on a healthy slow run and produced one wrong conclusion) and dumps every thread with :count >= 14 (frames 0-7 are interrupt plumbing) turned an hour of silence into a named stuck frame in minutes; sampling the SAME thread 4x at 3 s intervals distinguishes blocked from spinning, which ONE sample cannot. FOLLOW-ONS RECORDED NOT DONE: no permanent regression test (reproduction needs ~25 iterations / ~35 s, too slow for make test - belongs in a soak target, so this defect is currently guarded by an ADR and a counter, not a gate); 19 other dds.pal:join call sites remain UNBOUNDED; the flow-controller unregister emit barrier in stop-node is the other unbounded wait and is untouched. VERIFIED: 618/618 SBCL and Clasp, corpus 0 mismatches both, gate-hotpath/types/pal/nocond/drivers PASS, gate-mem 1739.6 vs ceiling 1775, gate-build clean-cache PASS both impls.

Notes: ADR 0092, closing the follow-ons ADR 0091 recorded rather than fixed. NINETEEN unbounded waits existed outside the test suite: 15 production dds.pal:join call sites (DCPS deadline monitor + autodiscovery announcer, dds-log async worker + runner drains + supervisor monitor, the SHMEM receive thread, durability collect/discovery-poll/process-monitor/supervisor-watcher/microservice accept+serve, the WP-ASYNC sender, the flow-control scheduler), 2 in-file test-harness joins, and 2 copies of the flow-controller per-node emit barrier. Any of them could stop a process forever at 0% CPU exactly as the UDP receiver did. ⚠️ THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE ONE DOCUMENTED ITSELF AS BOUNDED: the emit barrier's comment said 'bounded: re-check on wake, teardown can't wedge' and its docstring said 'the wait is bounded + re-checked so a logic error cannot wedge teardown forever' - BOTH FALSE. Only the inner condvar-wait was bounded, at 0.5 s; the LOOP WHILE around it retried forever, so a current-emit-node that never clears hangs teardown permanently at ~2 wakes/second. A WAIT ASSEMBLED FROM BOUNDED WAITS IS NOT ITSELF BOUNDED - and this is the second ADR running in which a docstring's confident claim was the thing standing between us and the bug (ADR 0091: udp-close's 'TRUE ON DARWIN'). BOUNDING IS THE EASY HALF. The hard half is what a timeout MEANS, and it is not 'carry on': nearly every one of these joins exists so a SUBSEQUENT release is safe - a free-static, a shm-detach, a store-close, a delete-participant, a socket close - so a join that cannot prove the thread stopped must SKIP that release. Answering 'is it bounded' without answering 'what does it guard' converts a hang into a USE-AFTER-FREE, which is strictly worse because the hang is at least loud and local. Each site was therefore classified by what it guards: :shmem-receiver skips pshared-destroy/shm-detach/shm-destroy (the receiver parks on a condvar INSIDE the segment - destroying it is a SIGSEGV in foreign code, not a leak); :flow-unregister and :flow-remove-writer make stop-node return early and free NOTHING; :flow-scheduler skips the SCRATCH free-static (the scheduler BUILDS datagrams into SCRATCH); :dcps-auto-announcer and :dcps-deadline-monitor skip the whole delete-participant (the announcer SENDS through the node's announce buffers; a deadline miss reaches an application listener that may write); :log-async-worker skips close-logger's delete-participant; :log-runner-drain skips PER INDEX because COLLECTORS and THREADS are parallel vectors, so one wedged drain costs only its own collector; :log-supervisor-monitor skips log-runner-stop entirely because a live monitor RESPAWNS drain threads onto collectors being closed; :durability-collect skips per node pair; :microservice-accept-loop skips the listener tcp-close (it is parked in accept(2), and a reused fd number would be accepted on by the wrong socket). TWO SITES REPORT AND PROCEED, deliberately: the durability supervisor watcher (refusing to stop the runner would skip every service-stop and therefore every store-close, LOSING THE FSYNC OF DURABLE STATE - data integrity outranks a stranded thread, and nothing is freed under a live thread either way because service-stop gates its own store-close on its own collect joins) and the process-service monitor (it only polls process-alive-p and owns no store, node or buffer). THE REPORT LIVES INSIDE join-bounded, at the point of DETECTION, not in a counter per owning struct: eight more struct fields would have duplicated the same field eight times and made the report OPTIONAL AT EVERY CALL SITE, in a codebase whose prevailing idiom for these joins was (ignore-errors (dds.pal:join th)) - i.e. discarding the result. Counting where the timeout is detected makes it impossible to forget and gives every future teardown wait the same reporting for free. REPORTED, NEVER PRINTED: stuck-teardown-joins returns (values TOTAL ALIST), a queryable snapshot in the same shape as logger-shed-counts and disc-node-stuck-receiver-teardowns. THE TWO TEST HARNESSES GET DELIBERATELY GENEROUS SITE-SPECIFIC DEADLINES (shmem-stress-tx = its own deadline-seconds + 30, za2-concur = 60) because a blanket 5 s there would fail a HEALTHY run - the point of a test-harness bound is only to turn an infinite hang into a failed assertion. A LATENT DEFECT FOUND WHILE WIRING THIS: stop-node's ADR 0091 early return was (return-from stop-node node) while its declaimed ftype is (function (disc-node) (eql t)) - under (safety 0) a caller compiled against that declaration may assume T; corrected. FALSIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS, each seen RED: with *join-timeout-seconds* set to NIL and current-emit-node pinned, the barrier is STILL BLOCKED AFTER 8 s and returns IMMEDIATELY once the predicate is released (proving it was blocked on the predicate, not dead) - the pre-fix behaviour reproduced on demand; and a wedged SHMEM receiver makes shmem-transport-close return :TIMEOUT, leave rx-thread set so the close is retryable, and leave the segment MAPPED AND READABLE THROUGH ITS SAP, proving the three destroy steps were skipped. PERMANENT REGRESSION TEST (teardown-deadline, 1.6 s, four legs): a clean join reports NOTHING (no false positives - a bound that counted every join would make the counter worthless); a wedged thread yields :TIMEOUT and is counted UNDER ITS OWN SITE KEYWORD (the report must say WHICH wait failed); the emit barrier TERMINATES, asserted on ELAPSED TIME rather than only on the return value; and a real participant create+delete moves the report by ZERO. VERIFIED: 619/619 SBCL and Clasp, corpus 13+1 with 0 mismatches on both impls, gate-build clean-cache PASS on both, gate-hotpath/types(3177 defuns)/pal/nocond(0 to go)/drivers PASS, fuzz PASS, gate-mem 1739 vs ceiling 1775 (unchanged - every edit is on a cold teardown path).

Notes: ADR 0093 SLICE 1, the first vertical slice of the OWNER'S DECISION (2026-07-28) to take Option 1: extend the loan contract to the copy path so NFR-MEM's 0 B/sample is reachable on the path gate-mem actually measures. THE BLOCKER WAS SEMANTIC, NOT EFFORT: the copy-path drain hands the application a RETAINED heap struct plus a sample-info, a cached-sample and a cache cons, and you cannot pool an object whose lifetime the application controls - DDS read is non-destructive, so the app may hold indefinitely. Making the lifetime EXPLICIT is what a loan is. MEASURED -171 B/sample (arm64 SBCL payload 0, 3 runs per arm): baseline-no-return 1738.8; application returns with pooling OFF 1739.2 (1737.6/1742.3/1737.7); pooling ON 1568.1 (1569.5/1567.2/1567.6). Ranges nowhere near overlapping. THE RETURN-LOAN CALL ITSELF IS FREE - baseline and pooling-OFF agree within noise, so the whole delta is the recycling, not the API. AS BUILT: take-samples hands back wrappers the app returns via return-loan; a returned wrapper is parked on a per-reader simple-vector pool and reused. return-loan gains a THIRD dispatch arm beside the FlatData-view and secured-handle arms, and DELEGATES to them for a wrapper that wraps a loan, so each loan kind keeps exactly ONE release path and returning a wrapper can never strand the loan it wrapped. THE PAIR IS POOLED AS ONE OBJECT - a parked wrapper keeps its sample-info attached, so one pop yields both and nothing is consed to link them. SHOULD, NOT MUST: a missed return degrades gracefully (the pool is empty, the next delivery allocates, i.e. exactly the pre-slice behaviour), so this is NOT a breaking change and the ~50 existing take-samples call sites keep working unmigrated - the migration promised in the ADR's own section 6 turned out to be a per-site BENEFIT, not a correctness prerequisite, and the ADR now says so. THREE FINDINGS THE MEASUREMENT PRODUCED, NONE OF THEM IN THE PLAN: (1) A LIST FREELIST ATE A FIFTH OF ITS OWN WIN - push/pop conses 2 conses = 32 B/sample against a ~144 B prize (1600.1 with lists vs 1568.1 with a simple-vector stack); a pool whose bookkeeping allocates is not a pool. The pool is also CAPPED (*rx-wrapper-pool-capacity* 64) because steady state needs ONE and an unbounded freelist is a leak wearing an optimisation's clothes. (2) THE A/B LEVER LEAKED WHILE IT WAS OFF - %recycle ran unconditionally while acquire was gated, so every return pushed onto a pool nothing drew from: unbounded growth AND a measured +33.5 B/sample, visible only because the OFF arm was MEASURED rather than assumed. A lever must be a true no-op on BOTH ends or it is not an A/B; the test now asserts exactly that. (3) ⚠️ A MEASUREMENT THAT WAS SIMPLY WRONG: an early three-arm run put the pooled arm at 2786 B/sample against a 1739 baseline - a 1000 B REGRESSION from a change that only removes allocation - and I began diagnosing it as a code defect. It was HARNESS CROSS-TALK: all three arms ran in ONE image on ONE domain (7), so each arm's participants discovered the previous arms' and paid for their traffic. One process per arm on distinct domains, the same code measured 1569.5. This is exactly the owner's standing order (concurrently running tests MUST use different DDS domain IDs), issued the same day. WHEN A NUMBER MOVES IN A WAY THE CHANGE CANNOT EXPLAIN, SUSPECT THE HARNESS'S ISOLATION BEFORE THE CODE. THE CORRECTNESS RISK IS NOT THE BYTES - it is a PARTIALLY RE-INITIALISED recycled struct handing the application a PREVIOUS sample's field: silent, application-visible, and invisible to any allocation gate, which measures bytes not meaning. So there is EXACTLY ONE initialisation path (a recycled sample-info is reused uninitialised and all 13 slots are then assigned unconditionally, including the three ranks nothing else writes; a separate fresh-vs-recycled field list would drift the first time a slot is added) and the test POISONS all 13 slots on a parked struct and asserts none survives the next delivery. ⭐ THE TEST OBSERVES THE STRUCT AT DRAIN TIME, NOT THROUGH TAKE: %select-samples legitimately RE-STAMPS sample_state, view_state and instance_state at SELECTION (DDS 1.4 section 2.2.2.5.4 requires the instance-level states to be computed when samples are returned, not frozen at delivery), so testing through take would have covered only 10 of the 13 slots WHILE APPEARING TO COVER ALL OF THEM. FALSIFIED, each seen RED: dropping ONE slot from the reinit turns :adr93-no-stale-sn red and nothing else; making acquire never recycle turns :adr93-reused red. ⚠️ THE WIN IS DELIBERATELY NOT RATCHETED: gate-mem's default workload does not return loans so it cannot see this win, and flipping that default re-baselines BOTH arch rows - only arm64 was measured, and the standing rule is that a row may be lowered only on the arch it was measured on (a predicted x86_64 number was already 58 B wrong once). Flipping mem-per-sample's :return-loans default and lowering both rows needs an x86_64 measurement; recorded as a follow-up, not done. VERIFIED: 620/620 SBCL and Clasp, gate-build clean-cache PASS both, corpus 13+1 0 mismatches both, gate-hotpath/types(3184)/pal/nocond/drivers PASS, gate-mem unchanged at 1740.

Notes: ADR 0093 SLICE 2 — the N>=2 remaining-consumers refcount (hazard 4). FIXES A REAL PRE-EXISTING LEAK, not just a pooling prerequisite: node-consume-sample was gated on node-sole-consumer-p, which refused to purge whenever TWO same-topic readers shared the participant's receive store - correct (reader-B still got its sample) but one-sided, because those samples were then retained FOREVER. That is exactly the unbounded leak AND the O(stored) drain that node-consume-sample exists to prevent (%drain rebuilds its pending-key list from the WHOLE store on every take, so a long-running multi-reader participant got monotonically slower), reinstated for every multi-reader participant. AS BUILT: a per-(GUID,SN) count table disc-node-sample-consumers, written at the store site from (length routes) - the same set the secured path already uses for its return-count - and decremented in node-consume-sample, which purges only on the LAST drain. ⚠️ RECORDED ONLY WHEN K >= 2: with one consumer the entry is ABSENT, the purge is immediate, and the overwhelmingly common case is byte-identical at zero cost (an absent entry means ONE consumer, never zero). The count is dropped at %purge-secured-sample, the single choke every (GUID,SN) entry leaves through, so it cannot outlive the sample it counts. %drain-one-sample now purges UNCONDITIONALLY - the multi-reader question moved out of DCPS and into the engine, where the store actually lives. BIAS: over-counting only re-leaks; under-counting would DELETE a sample a reader had not yet drained (silent loss), so ROUTES - a superset of the true drainers - is the safe side to err on, the same ranking the ZC %count-eligible-drainers applies. node-sole-consumer-p is KEPT as an exported query but now gates nothing; its docstring says so rather than leaving a stale claim. Notes: ADR 0093 SLICE 3 — hazard 2, and it was NOT merely 'unproven': it was a live data race with NO lock anywhere on the DataReader. The reader cache was built on two claims, BOTH FALSE: %drain's docstring said both streams are drained on the user thread 'so the reader cache + instance-recs are never mutated off-thread (S2)', and dr-keyhash-scratch's said the take path is 'single-threaded-per-reader'. dr-cache is setf/nconc'd at ~10 sites from THREE independent thread contexts: (1) the application thread via read/take/samples-available, all of which %drain; (2) whatever thread calls wait-set-wait - its trigger predicate %count-matching %drains too, and WS-LOCK excludes no taker because a taker never acquires it; (3) the discovery/announcer thread - %on-disc-unmatch -> %on-writer-vanished and, in AUTONOMOUS mode where SPIN is driven by the participant's own announcer thread, %spin-once -> %autopurge-sweep, both of which rewrite dr-cache and the instance-recs. FIXED with a per-reader cache lock (%with-reader-cache) taken by %drain, %select-samples, return-loan, take-loaned/read-loaned, samples-available, both WaitSet predicates, %on-writer-vanished and %autopurge-sweep. LOCK ORDER: cache lock OUTER, node lock INNER - %drain takes the node lock inside it; safe against the discovery path precisely because dds.disc fires ON-UNMATCH *outside* the node lock (%prune-participant-locked hands its removed matches out first), so nothing takes the node lock and then the cache lock. NOT RECURSIVE, so the two callers that arrive already holding it - the KEEP_LAST loan drop inside %drain, and return-loan recursing into a wrapper's backing loan - go through %return-loan-unlocked. DRAIN AND SELECT ARE TWO SEPARATE CRITICAL SECTIONS, DELIBERATELY: the safety property needed is only that no list mutation interleaves with another and that a wrapper handed to the application is out of the cache before it can be recycled, and both hold per-section; holding one lock across a whole read/take would serialise more for no safety gain. Two concurrent takers may each miss samples the other got - DDS never promised otherwise - but neither corrupts. ⚠️ THIS WAS NOT ONLY A SLICE-4 PREREQUISITE: SLICE 1 HAD ALREADY TURNED IT INTO A CRASH. Before slice 1 the race lost or duplicated samples; after it, %recycle-delivery clears a returned wrapper's DATA, so a concurrent taker still holding that wrapper reads NIL. Falsified exactly so: with the lock removed the test dies with 'Unhandled TYPE-ERROR ... The value NIL is not of type SHAPE-TYPE' on a taker thread, followed by a FATAL sig10 in a non-lisp thread - the process does not survive. So commits 3aed0a1..508ae5e carry a narrow crash window for an application that BOTH takes from two threads on one reader AND returns its loans; narrow, but real, and introduced by this work rather than inherited. TEST reader-cache-race: two threads take from ONE reader while a writer publishes 200 keyed samples; the union must be EXACTLY those 200 with NO duplicate (a lost sample = an interleaved cache rewrite; a duplicate = both threads selected the same cached-sample before either removed it). VERIFIED: 622/622 SBCL and Clasp, gate-build clean-cache PASS both, corpus 13+1 0 mismatches, gate-hotpath/types(3190)/pal/nocond/drivers PASS, GATE-MEM UNCHANGED (COPY 1741.2 / RETURN 1567.4) - the lock costs no allocation.

Notes: A RETURN-FROM OUT OF A HANDLER-CASE NESTED IN A LOCK COSTS 16 B ON EVERY CALL, INCLUDING EVERY CALL THAT NEVER ENTERS THE BRANCH. Four DDS-Security zero-alloc gates were red on Linux x86_64 and green on macOS/arm64: secured-live-zeroalloc (LIVE-RX-LOAN-ZERO-DELTA-256, +16.2472 B/sample), rtps-protection-zeroalloc (16.38 B/datagram), user-submessage-protection-zeroalloc (16.38 B/datagram) and secured-dataplane-mem (T5 meta-send delta 16.3840). They had been INVISIBLE because Ubuntu 24.04 ships OpenSSL 3.0.x, dare-available-p returned NIL and the WHOLE DDS-Security suite SKIPPED on Linux - every 'N passed, 0 FAILED' Linux run before 2026-07-29 was not covering it. TWO EXPLANATIONS RULED OUT FIRST, either of which would have ended the hunt: (1) NOT a TLAB artifact - 16.384 = 65536/4000 exactly, i.e. one 64 KiB refill over the gate's 4000 iterations, so the gate's own number cannot distinguish a per-call cost from a one-off; an iteration sweep settles it (1000->0.0000, 4000->16.3840, 16000->16.3840, 64000->16.3840, 256000->16.0000, converging on the TRUE flat per-call cost). (2) NOT the crypto - piece-by-piece inside %maybe-wrap-srtps at 200k iters each, encode-rtps-message-into (the AEAD itself) 0.0000, pool acquire+release 0.0000, %with-send-scratch 0.0000, while %ensure-send-scratch-pool alone measured 15.8925 - a function whose steady-state path is ONLY (or (slot node) <untaken carve>), a struct-slot read that cannot cons. THE LADDER THAT NAMED IT: v1 slot read 0.0000, v2 + untaken WITH-LOCK 0.0000, v3 + untaken HANDLER-CASE 0.0000, v4 + untaken HANDLER-CASE containing a RETURN-FROM 0.0000, v5 all three NESTED 16.0563, v6 the same nesting with the RETURN-FROM removed 0.0000, v7 the candidate fix (WHEN-guarded SETF) 0.0000, REAL %ensure-send-scratch-pool (in-process control) 16.0563. v5 and v6 differ by ONE TOKEN. MECHANISM: dds.pal:with-lock expands to an UNWIND-PROTECT and HANDLER-CASE installs a handler closure that is normally stack-allocated; a RETURN-FROM targeting a block OUTSIDE the intervening UNWIND-PROTECT means the non-local exit must run through the unwind, the closure loses dynamic extent, and a no-capture SBCL closure on x86_64 is 2 words = 16 B, built at function ENTRY and therefore charged to every call. FIX: the RETURN-FROM was GRATUITOUS at all nine sites - NIL propagates out through the enclosing OR/WITH-LOCK/OR chain to the identical result - so it becomes a WHEN-guarded SETF, semantically identical with no NLX. The ADR 0064 obligation it discharged (a NIL pool MUST be tested or the SETF stores an arena the contract says to store only after a successful carve) is UNCHANGED; the guard tests it without unwinding. At %ensure-secured-payload-pool the change is also a CORRECTNESS improvement: its RETURN-FROM unwound out of a callback through writer-ensure-payload-pool's writer lock and out of that function entirely, whereas returning NIL is that function's DOCUMENTED provision-fn contract ('or NIL when no pool could be carved'), already handled by its (when pool (setf ...)) pool body. MEASURED red-to-green on Linux x86_64: secured-live-zeroalloc RX-loan@256 +16.2472 -> +0.1579, rtps-protection-zeroalloc SRTPS wrap 16.38 -> 0.00 B/datagram, secured-dataplane-mem meta-send delta 16.3840 -> 0.0000 (and rtps-send/rtps-recv/oauth-send all 0.0000); FULL SUITE 620 passed/4 FAILED/624 -> 624 passed/0 FAILED/624. No new compiler warnings (the 4 undefined-variable forward references are byte-identical to a stashed-baseline compile of the same two files). NOT CLAIMED TO BE x86_64-SPECIFIC, and the data cannot support that: the dev box is SBCL 2.6.5 on arm64 while the repro image deliberately runs the Ubuntu distro SBCL on x86_64 to match CI, so BOTH arch and compiler version differ. It does not matter for the fix - the construct is removed outright, so the cost is zero on every implementation and the property no longer depends on which compiler notices it. arm64 gate-mem is EXPECTED UNCHANGED and both arm64 columns in bench/mem-ceiling.txt are deliberately LEFT ALONE - this is not an arm64 allocation slice. THE METHODOLOGICAL LESSON: NO SINGLE CONSTRUCT IN THIS SHAPE ALLOCATES. Testing them one at a time - the obvious experiment - returns 0.0000 four times and exonerates the real cause; only the COMPOSITION allocates, so the ladder must include the composed shape or it proves nothing. ALSO OPEN, NOT CLOSED BY THIS SLICE: the shape had been copied NINE times and nothing stops a tenth. The borrow half of this pair is already factored (%with-scratch with thin per-pool wrappers); the carve half should be too - a separate, behaviour-free DRY slice.

Notes: THE DRY HALF OF ADR 0098, LANDED AS A SEPARATE BEHAVIOUR-FREE SLICE. The nine-fold duplication was WHY one construct produced four independent red gates, and nothing stopped a tenth copy reintroducing it. %lazy-carve-pool now holds the whole invariant in ONE place: carve exactly once, off the steady state, under the pool's own lock; on failure leave the slot NIL and change nothing; NEVER unwind. It is the carve twin of %with-scratch (the shared BORROW), and lives beside it. Parameters: the pool/lock/arena disc-node accessor NAMES, element-bytes and capacity, an optional :conditions (default ERROR; sites whose allocation can exhaust real off-heap memory pass (or error storage-condition), which is what a static-alloc OOM signals on SBCL and Clasp), an optional :on-failure (the one site that LATCHES its carve failure rather than retrying per sample), and an optional INSTALL body run inside the lock only after a successful carve with the pool bound. It sets the arena slot and then the pool slot, pool LAST, because that slot IS the double-checked-carve flag. EIGHT OF NINE converted: send-scratch, submsg-scratch, zc-overlay-scratch, secured-decode, rx-store (dataplane.lisp) and secure-rx, bracket-rx, key-id-rx (disc.lisp). %ensure-secured-payload-pool is a DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION - its pool lives on the WRITER's HistoryCache rather than a node slot, its double-check and lock belong to writer-ensure-payload-pool, and its arena is pushed onto a LIST under a different lock, so it shares the guarded carve but NOT the structure. Covering it would require making the pool slot, the lock AND the arena slot all optional, which buys one call site and costs every reader of the macro; the macro's docstring names the exception so it stays a decision instead of decaying into an oversight. VERIFIED BY MACROEXPANSION, not by assertion: a simple site expands to exactly the hand-written double-checked shape, and the fully-parameterised site expands with INSTALL first inside the WHEN, then the arena slot, then the pool slot, with the guard running ON-FAILURE and yielding NIL. ONE BEHAVIOURAL DIFFERENCE, deliberate and strictly-less-work: %ensure-secured-decode-pool's handle vector was previously allocated in the let* BEFORE the pool-NIL test, i.e. allocated and discarded on a FAILED carve; it now allocates inside the install body, so a failed carve does not build it. Still inside the guard, so a storage-condition from it is caught exactly as before. Net effect on the two source files: 113 insertions / 135 deletions, and the insertions are mostly the macro's docstring - dataplane.lisp alone is -46 lines. NOT A PERFORMANCE CHANGE and not claimed as one: gate-mem x3 unchanged, both arm64 ceilings in bench/mem-ceiling.txt deliberately untouched. WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY, stated so it is not over-credited: the macro protects the sites that USE it, not the language. A hand-written tenth carve, or a RETURN-FROM added inside any other HANDLER-CASE nested in an UNWIND-PROTECT on a per-sample path, is still unguarded. The construct-level protection would be a GATE - a checker that reads the forms and fails on that nesting - and it is OPEN, not done here.

Notes: A SHARED-MEMORY SEGMENT BELONGS TO A DOMAIN, NOT JUST TO A PARTICIPANT (owner directive 2026-07-30: 'SHMEM resolution MUST also be domain-dependent'). %seg-name derived the shm receive-segment name from the GUID PREFIX ALONE. A POSIX shm name is a PROCESS-GLOBAL, HOST-GLOBAL OS object while a DDS domain is an ISOLATION BOUNDARY (DDS 1.4 2.2.1.2.2), so two participants sharing a GuidPrefix in DIFFERENT DOMAINS resolved to the SAME segment and exchanged datagrams across a boundary the spec says must isolate them. WHY IT HAD NEVER BEEN SEEN, and the precise reason: UDP is domain-scoped BY CONSTRUCTION - each domain computes its own port range from domain_id (RTPS 2.5 9.6.1.1) - so the PORT was the isolation and SHMEM inherited no equivalent. As long as all control traffic went over UDP the collision was unreachable. FIX: the domain is part of the segment identity - '/dds<10hex token>d<domain hex>' - and every derivation site passes it: the receive segment (make-shmem-transport), the sender's resolve (%resolve-shmem-dest) and the Zero-Copy pool segment (%zc-pool-name, ADR 0014, which inherits the scoping so a ZC slot cannot be read across a domain either). Sender and receiver compute the same name from the same two inputs and a sample only reaches a reader in the writer's domain, so the two sides always agree. Name budget 19 chars + the ZC 'z' = 20, under the macOS ~31-char cap. HOW IT WAS FOUND: while root-causing ADR 0097, which was BLOCKED by this defect. run-access-control-allow-deny-test failed deterministically with ADR 0097 and passed without it; a single-variable A/B (one runtime switch, one binary, the same probe in both arms) confirmed the control-lane routing as the trigger. THREE HYPOTHESES KILLED BY MEASUREMENT: the node lock is non-recursive but %push-heartbeat is not called under it; raising the RX pool capacity 8->256 changed nothing; and the 354-vs-2 heartbeat ratio was a CONSEQUENCE (an unacked HistoryCache never purges so the periodic HEARTBEAT keeps firing), not a cause. The finding came from printing the FULL 12-octet prefixes: sq-a and ci-a were both D1437B8E7A950708090A0B0C and sq-b and ci-b both B9A1E95FB45E0708090A0B0C - two participants per side, on two different domains, sharing one GuidPrefix and therefore one segment. MEASURED: 5/5 FAIL -> 5/5 PASS with ADR 0097 enabled and the TEST UNMODIFIED (3/3 PASS with ADR 0097 reverted, i.e. the baseline was never exercising the collision). ADR 0097 IS UNBLOCKED AND WAS NOT AT FAULT: it did not introduce a defect, it became the first traffic to depend on SHMEM honouring the domain boundary. Its measured benefit (2249 -> 800 writer datagrams for 400 samples, +181 percent traffic saved) stands; landing it is a separate slice. NOT FIXED, stated so it is not over-credited: %guid-token folds only prefix octets 0..7, so two prefixes in the SAME domain differing only in octets 8..11 still collide - a pre-existing narrowing of a 12-octet identifier to 8, documented at seg-name-for-guid and left OPEN because bundling it would have made this measurement unattributable. ABI: the segment name changes, so a domain-scoped sender and an unscoped receiver never meet and fall back to UDP - correct delivery, lost optimisation, no corruption; mixed-version same-host peers are the only affected case. A TAGGING MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING, because it produced a wrong PUBLISHED conclusion: the first probe tagged participants by prefix octets 2..3, then 8..11, and BOTH are uniform across all four participants in this test; a lane-divergence diagnosis was reported on that basis and had to be RETRACTED. A probe that cannot distinguish the entities it labels does not report 'unknown', it reports a confident WRONG answer - print the whole identifier or prove the short form injective. Notes: ADR 0099 SECTION 3 CLOSED: %guid-token folded only GUID-prefix octets 0..7, narrowing a 12-octet identifier to 8. Now FNV-1a 64 over ALL TWELVE octets (folding a zero hash to 1, since 0 marks a free lane). IT WAS WORSE THAN THE 'SAME SEGMENT NAME' ADR 0099 ORIGINALLY RECORDED, and that is the finding: the token is not only the segment name, it is ALSO THE LANE OWNER — %claim-lane returns an existing lane on (= owner token). Two participants whose prefixes differed only in octets 8..11 would therefore have been handed THE SAME LANE in the receiver's ring: two independent senders writing into one single-producer lane. That is a CORRUPTION hazard, not a lost optimisation, and it is the more dangerous of the two ADR 0099 defects even though it is the one that never showed up in a test — which is exactly why 'documented and left open' was the right call for one slice and the wrong place to stop. MEASURED distinctness on the exact collision case: prefixes 01..0B0C and 01..0B0D (differing ONLY in octet 11) now yield 222D454F170E2075 vs 222D444F170E1EC2; prefixes differing in octets 0..7 stay distinct; the token is nonzero. NAME LENGTH re-checked against the cap that motivated the original truncation: '/dds' + up to 16 hex + 'd' + up to 4 hex = 25, plus the ZC pool's 'z' suffix = 26, under the macOS ~31-char shm-name cap (measured at domain 65535, the worst case). FNV-1a is chosen for being trivially correct over 12 octets, NOT for cryptographic strength: nothing here is adversarial, since a peer that can already open the segment needs no hash collision to disrupt it. Cold path — computed once per segment create / per peer resolve; the send path reads the memoized SHMEM-TRANSPORT-TOKEN slot. ABI: the segment name changes again (as it did for ADR 0099). A mismatched pair simply never meets and falls back to UDP — correct delivery, lost optimisation, no corruption. ⚠️ AN UNRELATED PRE-EXISTING INTERMITTENT WAS DISCOVERED AND CORRECTLY ATTRIBUTED, NOT ASSUMED: async-emit-fault-survives (ASYNC-FAULT-DELIVERED, 'all 6 samples must still be delivered') failed in the macOS suite. Notes: THE SHMEM ATTACH CACHE WAS SHARED MUTABLE STATE WITH NO LOCK (owner directive 2026-07-30: 'do (a) + (c) with a before/after bench'). %attach-for did an UNLOCKED gethash and an UNLOCKED (setf gethash) on ONE table per node, reached from FOUR THREADS — the publishing thread, the async sender, the receiver thread running the ACKNACK repair, and the flow-control scheduler — on EVERY %shmem-send. The docstring's 'off the hot path' was true of the ATTACH and false of the LOOKUP. TWO HARMS, ONE SILENT: (1) concurrent mutation broke SBCL's internal hash-table invariants, which SBCL reported as `failed AVER: (= HWM (HASH-TABLE-PAIRS-CAPACITY ...))`; (2) two threads racing the same NEW peer each ran shm-attach and one clobbered the other, so the loser's mapping was never detached — a leak. BOTH WERE ABSORBED by %send-raw-buf's self-guard into a quiet UDP fallback plus a counter nobody asserted on, so SHMEM degraded and NO TEST EVER WENT RED. It surfaced only because a :shmem-send-fault fires the same global hook that a flaky test happened to be counting — i.e. it was found by accident, which is the argument for (c). (a) EVERY access is now under a new ATTACH-LOCK: the per-datagram lookup, the fill, and teardown's maphash/clrhash. The attach and lane-claim stay INSIDE the lock so two threads racing one new peer produce ONE attach and ONE lane claim. A double-checked unlocked fast read was CONSIDERED AND REJECTED — a reader concurrent with the rehash inside (setf gethash) is the same race with a narrower window. (c) dds.pal:internal-bug-p (new, per-impl: sb-int:bug on SBCL, NIL elsewhere as a documented NFR-PORT gap that restores exactly the old behaviour) splits the guard: an ordinary error still bumps SHMEM-SEND-FAULTS and falls back to UDP, while an internal-invariant violation bumps a DEDICATED counter, fires the hook with the DISTINCT context :SHMEM-INTERNAL-BUG, and LATCHES SHMEM OFF for the node so a possibly-corrupt cache is never consulted again. FAIL-SAFE, NOT FAIL-STOP: the datagram still falls back to UDP and the sender thread still survives — signalling there would kill it, which the operating contract forbids and which is strictly worse. What changes is that the event is loud, separately countable, and stops further use of the suspect structure. MEASURED (isolated %shmem-send primitive, 200000 sends of 64 octets, 3 runs, macOS/arm64): 106.1/106.3/107.6 -> 124.2/124.4/124.6 ns/send, i.e. +18 ns (~+17 percent) on the primitive, and 0.0000 B/send in BOTH arms. Reported even though it goes the WRONG way, because the contract requires a number for any hot-path change; the trade is correct under the ranking (correctness is a binary gate, performance is the optimisation target) and gate-mem is unchanged. IF THAT 18 ns IS EVER WORTH RECLAIMING: stop calling %attach-for per datagram — memoise the resolved shmem-dest on the locator the discovery layer already caches per peer (ADR 0067 does the analogous thing for the SAP and lane), leaving the lock on the cold fill path only. Deliberately NOT bundled with a correctness fix. THE TEST IS FALSIFIED, which is the only reason to believe a green concurrency test: with the lock removed and the test unchanged, 5 of 8 runs FAIL on 'all threads must share ONE dest ... (got 2 distinct)'; with the lock, 6 of 6 PASS. ⚠️ A data race is never REQUIRED to manifest, so the test cannot prove absence — it runs the race hard enough that a regression is likely caught, and asserts the invariant unsynchronised access cannot reliably maintain. ⚠️ THIS DOES NOT CLOSE the second async-emit-fault-survives failure mode (got 1 of 6, writer HC intact at SN 1..6, BOTH sides matched). That remains OPEN and must not be assumed fixed.

Notes: ADR 0095 SLICE 2 — STARTUP-ALLOCATED. %prealloc-node-pools runs in start-node BEFORE any receiver thread, so a pool carve lands at init instead of as a first-sample latency spike. This is the PRE-ALLOCATION half of the standing 0-B-with-full-arena-pre-allocation directive. IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CARVE EVERYTHING, and that is the design decision worth recording: eagerly carving every pool would cost a PLAIN node the megabytes of security scratch it will never touch, breaking the property each of those accessors explicitly documents ('a node with rtps_protection off reserves no static memory'). The predicates therefore MIRROR EXACTLY the gates the use sites test — rx-store when *rx-store-pool-enabled*; send-scratch on non-NONE rtps_protection; submsg-scratch on non-NONE metadata_protection; secure-rx/bracket-rx/key-id-rx when either wire tier is on; decode when a crypto-transform is installed. THE LAZY PATH REMAINS AND MUST: DDS-Security keys can arrive AFTER start-node via the live handshake (the crypto-manager installs them post-enable), so a node plain at startup and keyed later still carves on first use — which is exactly why %lazy-carve-pool (ADR 0098) double-checks under the lock. PRE-ALLOCATION IS AN OPTIMISATION OF WHEN, NEVER A CHANGE OF WHETHER. Two pools stay lazy BY NATURE and are named in the docstring: %ensure-secured-payload-pool (sized per WRITER from its HistoryCache, so it belongs to writer creation, not node creation) and %ensure-zc-overlay-scratch (needs a resolved EntityCrypto, ADR 0051). ASSERTED ON THE SLOT, NOT A TIMING PROXY, and FALSIFIED: gate-arena ARM 5 first proves that with *rx-store-pool-enabled* NIL, start-node carves NOTHING — so the positive assertion is reading a real slot and not something trivially always set — then proves the slot is non-NIL after start-node with it enabled. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, reported rather than buried: the gate's participant-pair high-water rose 2363824 -> 3413168 B (5.09 percent of the 64 MiB budget). That is memory RESERVED AT INIT rather than discovered mid-run, which is the entire point of pre-allocation — a node now learns at startup whether it has the memory instead of finding out on a sample. Notes: ADR 0095 SLICE 3 — THE BYPASS IS CLOSED. The long-lived receive/TX scratch came from bare dds.pal:alloc-static, so per node 3 x 65507 B of receiver-thread datagram buffers (~192 KiB — the figure the slice was written around) PLUS 2 x 65507 + 512 B of TX scratch (~128 KiB), about 328 KB, sat OUTSIDE *static-arena-bytes*. FR-PF-7's 'all hot-path memory comes from the static arena' was therefore false for its SINGLE LARGEST CONSUMER, and a budget that cannot see the biggest allocation bounds nothing. dds.core.arena:carve-buffer is implemented as a CAPACITY-1 BUFFER-POOL, deliberately: the pool already carries the budget charge, the RESERVED accounting and the teardown-arena return, so a dedicated buffer needs no second mechanism and cannot drift from the pool path as either evolves. OWNERSHIP MOVED AND THE TEARDOWN RULES MOVED WITH IT — the part most likely to go wrong. An arena-backed buffer is freed by teardown-arena and NEVER by its user; freeing it twice is a double free of STATIC memory. So the receiver thread frees only a SELF-allocated buffer (the OWNED flag) and stop-node skips the three free-static calls when SCRATCH-ARENA-BACKED. That is safe because stop-node JOINS every thread before tearing the arena down, and on a stuck join the existing teardown-leaked gate skips BOTH the frees and the teardown — buffer and arena leak together, exactly as the buffer alone did before, so the ADR 0092 safety ranking is preserved rather than weakened. ALL THREE TX BUFFERS OR NONE, because teardown frees them as a set and a partial carve would need per-buffer ownership bookkeeping for no benefit. A PARTIAL CARVE RETURNS ITS CHARGE (teardown-arena on the discarded sub-arena) — without that, a node that failed to pre-allocate would silently shrink the process budget for every node created after it. A refused carve keeps the original alloc-static path byte-identical: a tight budget DEGRADES, it never stops a node from starting. A BUG CAUGHT BY THE TYPE SYSTEM DURING THE SLICE, worth recording: (and buf-a buf-b buf-c) yields the last BUFFER, not T, and the ownership slot is declared BOOLEAN — the defstruct* type check rejected it immediately rather than letting a truthy octet-buffer masquerade as the flag. TESTED IN LISP, NOT IN THE GATE'S SHELL-EMBEDDED STRING: an ARM inside gate-arena.sh cost two rounds to paren-balance because the shell escaping (#'"'"'format) means the text SBCL reads is not the text in the file — a naive balance checker is unreliable there. run-arena-scratch-test is compiler-checked Lisp in the suite instead, which is the right home for an assertion this fiddly. FALSIFIED: forcing scratch-arena-p to NIL (the old bare alloc-static path) turns the test RED on ARENA-SCRATCH-BACKED. It asserts the ownership flag BY NAME so a future silent revert is caught, not merely an arithmetic coincidence in the byte delta. MEASURED: gate-arena's participant-pair high-water moved 3413168 -> 3938248 B (5.87 percent of the 64 MiB budget) — that delta IS the previously-invisible scratch, now charged and, per ARM 3, returned. Notes: ADR 0095 SLICE 4 — the END-TO-END exhaustion proof is shipped; the RESOURCE_LIMITS half is an OPEN OWNER DECISION and is recorded as such rather than quietly closed. SHIPPED: gate-arena ARM 1 already proved a single carve is REFUSED against a tiny budget, but nothing checked that a WHOLE NODE behaves when EVERY carve is refused AT ONCE — which is the only form of the question an operator ever meets. run-arena-exhaustion-test runs a node against a 4 KiB process budget so the slice-3 TX scratch, the slice-2 RX store pool and the receiver's datagram buffer are ALL refused, and asserts: the node still STARTS; it reports its scratch as NOT arena-backed (it took the documented alloc-static fallback rather than claiming a carve it never got); the RX store pool is ABSENT rather than silently carved outside the budget; and stop-node still returns cleanly — no double free of a buffer it never owned, which is the specific hazard slice 3's ownership split introduced. NOT SHIPPED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED: 'the engine maps it to RESOURCE_LIMITS' is NOT what the code does. On exhaustion every pool degrades to an allocating fallback, each defended in its own docstring as 'correct, byte-identical wire, never a per-datagram GC on the pooled path'. That is a DIRECT DIVERGENCE from this ADR's own wording AND from the operating contract's 'arena exhaustion -> RESOURCE_LIMITS (reject/backpressure), never a silent GC-heap fallback'. THE TWO READINGS ARE MATERIALLY DIFFERENT PRODUCTS, which is why it is an owner decision: DEGRADE (today) keeps a memory-constrained deployment delivering, on the GC heap, at lower performance — nothing is lost but the 0-B property; REJECT (as written) makes exhaustion backpressure, so the static-memory guarantee is absolute and the operator learns immediately, but data is DROPPED rather than degraded. The fallbacks are DOCUMENTED, not silent, so the contract's word 'silent' is arguably already satisfied — that is the strongest argument for the status quo and it is not mine to settle. THE TEST DELIBERATELY ASSERTS ONLY WHAT IS TRUE TODAY and says so in its own docstring, rather than being written to pass by asserting whatever the code happens to do. Notes: OWNER REQUIREMENT 2026-07-31: 'The Arena Manager must allow for arena growth in configurable chunks up until a configurable max arena size.' WHY IT COMES BEFORE ADR 0101: that ADR makes exhaustion a RESOURCE_LIMITS reject, and against a FIXED initial budget that is brutal — the process refuses work the moment its opening estimate is wrong. With growth, exhaustion means THE CONFIGURED MAXIMUM WAS REACHED rather than THE INITIAL RESERVATION WAS FULL, which is the difference between a ceiling an operator chose and a guess. THREE KNOBS: *static-arena-bytes* (initial reservation), *static-arena-growth-bytes* (the chunk a miss grows by; 0 DISABLES growth), *static-arena-max-bytes* (hard ceiling; equal to the initial budget restores the old behaviour exactly). Growth is asked of the BUDGET-HOLDER — a sub-arena is a charge account whose real ceiling is its parent's (ADR 0095 option (a)) — so make-buffer-pool grows CHARGE-TO, never the sub-arena. THE SAFETY ARGUMENT, which is specific to how this arena was built: GROWTH IS PURE ACCOUNTING. The arena is a BUDGET, not a slab — every buffer is its own dds.pal:alloc-static region and the arena tracks only budget-versus-used — so raising the budget allocates nothing, moves nothing, and CANNOT INVALIDATE AN ADDRESS AN EARLIER CARVE ALREADY HANDED OUT. The same operation on a bump allocator over one contiguous block would be a use-after-free waiting to happen. Any future arena that IS a real slab must not inherit this without re-deriving that argument. WHOLE CHUNKS, NOT EXACT FIT: growing by precisely what the current carve needs would turn every subsequent carve into another growth step, so the budget would creep upward one allocation at a time and the ceiling would stop being a meaningful operating signal. Growths are COUNTED (arena-growths) so the event is observable rather than silent. MEASURED: initial 4096 B + a 256 KiB carve -> budget 1052672 B, growths 1; the same carve with max 8192 -> :ARENA-EXHAUSTED with the budget stopped AT 8192; chunk 0 -> refused, budget untouched, zero growths; a carve just over budget -> exactly one full chunk. ⚠️ IT BROKE TWO EXISTING CHECKS BY DESIGN, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF HAVING THEM: gate-arena ARM 1 and run-arena-exhaustion-test both proved refusal by pinning a tiny *static-arena-bytes*. With growth that no longer exhausts anything — the arena simply grows past it — so both would have SILENTLY STOPPED TESTING EXHAUSTION WHILE STILL PASSING. Both now pin *static-arena-max-bytes* too. Exactly the failure mode the never-trust-an-unfalsified-gate rule exists for, caught because the gates were run. Notes: ADR 0101 SLICE 1 (owner ruling 2026-07-31: 'We do as the contract says — that is why it is a contract after all!'). The operating contract requires arena exhaustion to map to RESOURCE_LIMITS, never a silent GC-heap fallback; three RX paths degraded to heap allocation instead. Converted to drop+count via a new DISC-NODE-ARENA-REJECTS counter, which is what turns 'never a SILENT fallback' into something observable. For RELIABLE a drop IS the backpressure the contract asks for (unacked -> writer retransmits); for BEST_EFFORT a drop is conformant. The secured decode path already self-caps at the working-set budget and rejects there, so it was left unchanged. ORDERING NOTE: this is only defensible because ADR 0102 landed first — exhaustion now means the CONFIGURED MAXIMUM was reached, not that an opening estimate was wrong. Notes: ADR 0104 — A LIBC SYMBOL POINTER MUST NOT DEPEND ON WHICH CFFI IS LOADED. An INSTALLED Clasp ships no contrib lisp tree, so ASDF falls through to Quicklisp's CFFI, whose Clasp backend passes CFFI's :DEFAULT library marker straight to a primitive that does not know that keyword and returns NIL; Clasp's BUNDLED contrib CFFI translates it to :RTLD-DEFAULT and works. Same source, same Clasp version, same host, opposite behaviour - because the dependency resolved to a different copy. NOT an FFI defect and NOT a broken install: by-name foreign-funcall works throughout, so only projects that CACHE foreign symbol pointers are affected - this stack does so deliberately, because a by-name call re-resolves through dlsym on every call on Clasp (~3.8 us) which is intolerable per datagram. The atomics are the sharp edge: the three __atomic_* pointers behind the SHMEM lane claim and the Zero-Copy refcount resolve through the same call, so fixing only recvfrom would have shipped the next failure. dds-dare is unaffected (it dispatches on an explicit :library handle). Cache trap: two builds reporting one version string SHARE an ASDF output directory, so any A/B across them needs its own XDG_CACHE_HOME or it measures whichever compiled first.

Notes: ADR 0105 TASK 6a. DR-CACHE's SPINE cost one fresh cons per delivered sample - the wrapper has been pooled since ADR 0093, the cell holding it was not - and the take side then discarded the whole spine and rebuilt it from a KEEP list. %select-samples-unlocked now walks with a PREV pointer and UNLINKS each selected cell IN PLACE, parking it on a per-reader free list that the next delivery pops straight back; the un-selected keep their cells and their arrival order, so nothing is rebuilt and nothing is reversed. THE INTRUSIVE ALTERNATIVE WAS REJECTED ON A MEASURED GROUND, not taste: a next slot on cached-sample would be its FIFTH, and SBCL/arm64 measures a 4-slot defstruct at 47.8 B against a 5-slot one at 64.2 B (the same finding that packed data-pinned and was-exposed into one flags slot in Task 2); the COPY arm allocates a wrapper per sample because it never returns a loan, so a fifth slot would cost it +16 B/sample and cancel this win exactly - net zero on COPY, -16 on RETURN. Pooling cells wins on BOTH arms. Notes: ADR 0108. The DCPS drain's exactly-once record was a per-writer HIGH-WATER MARK, which answers 'already delivered' for every SN below itself - so a reordered lower SN (routine under concurrent writes on one DataWriter, permitted by DDS 1.4 2.2.2.4.2.11) was skipped FOREVER while sitting undrained in the reader's node store, violating RELIABILITY 2.2.3.14. Replaced by a CIRCULAR 1024-bit delivered-set window (the RFC 4303 Appendix A2 anti-replay shape): high-water plus a 16-word bitmap indexed by SN mod width, advancing CLEARS the bits it scrolls past rather than shifting. Measured UDP 93-96 of 120 -> 120/120. WIDTH FROM MEASUREMENT: observed reorder depth was 90, and the FIRST attempt's 30-bit shifted-fixnum window left UDP at 101-111 for exactly that reason (see ADR 0108 sections 7-8; it was reverted, then revived widened). Cost is per matched WRITER (one cons + 128 octets), never per sample; the in-order case decides on the first comparison and never reads the bitmap. THE ZC JOIN-WATERMARK REMAINS A SEPARATE CONJUNCT - dds-disc counts eligible ZC drainers with SN > wm ALONE and is safe only because every DCPS drainer also satisfies it (superset, disc.lisp:895); folding it in would break a memory-safety argument silently. FALSIFIED BOTH WAYS: reverting %drained-delivered-p to a bare high-water turns DW-REORDERED-PENDING red; deleting the clear-on-advance turns DW-WRAP-NOT-STALE red. An earlier wrap fixture stayed GREEN under that second sabotage because it advanced a FULL window width and took the wholesale-reset branch, never reaching the clear loop - the fixture now advances twice, each strictly inside one width.

Notes: ADR 0109. %LANE-ENQUEUE IS A SINGLE-PRODUCER RING AND THE SEND PATH HAD MANY PRODUCERS. It reads the write cursor, memcpys the record at that position and publishes cursor+span - three non-atomic steps - and %shmem-send called it with NO mutual exclusion. A lane is claimed per SENDER TOKEN (the participant GUID prefix), so every thread of one participant shares ONE lane: the publisher, the async sender, the receiver thread's ACKNACK repair, the flow scheduler, and every application thread calling write. Two producers resolve the same ring position, the second memcpy DESTROYS the first record, and the cursor advances by one span for two writes - a datagram lost outright with no reordering involved, and when the spans differ a consumer that resumes MID-RECORD and decodes a datagram header as a SerializedPayload (observed: unknown representation id 0x5254, and 0x52 0x54 is 'RT', the RTPS magic). ADR 0100 locked the attach CACHE on this same path and left the enqueue itself unlocked. Fixed with a lock on the DESTINATION (one per lane, so sends to different peers stay concurrent), NOT held across the futex wake, and with no non-local exit crossing it (ADR 0098). Corruption: 1 run in 5 before, none in 40+ trials after. NEITHER FIX IS SUFFICIENT ALONE - ADR 0109 alone removes the corruption but leaves 102/110/53/110/114; ADR 0108 alone measured as no improvement at all, which is why its first attempt was reverted.

Notes: ADR 0112, THE THIRD AND LAST DEFECT IN THE CONCURRENT-WRITE WORKLOAD. %push-data assembles the outgoing RTPS message ON THE CALLING THREAD into disc-node-tx-msg - ONE octet-buffer slot on the node - through the single tx-cursor paired with it. DDS 1.4 2.2.2.4.2.11 permits any number of concurrent writers, so N application threads interleaved their datagram assembly into one buffer. THE CODE STATED THE INVARIANT IT WAS VIOLATING: %push-data-buf's docstring says 'each thread owns its buffer' and tx-cursor's says the receiver threads each have their own 'because they run concurrently with each other and with this one' - one-buffer-per-thread was applied to every thread the design ENUMERATED (receiver threads, the async sender with its own async-tx-msg) and application threads were never enumerated. ONE MECHANISM EXPLAINS EVERY SYMPTOM collected across the whole investigation: a second thread's message HEADER inside the first's payload (the reader decoding the RTPS magic RT as representation id 0x5254, also 0x0207/0x0205/0x0701/0x2800), a length read out of interleaved bytes (buffer-overflow need 117440512 = 0x07000000), and one sample's octets under another's sequence number (one instance delivered TWICE while another never arrives). It also explains why the payload-integrity assertion was blind: a mis-attributed sample is a COMPLETE, SELF-CONSISTENT sample carried under the wrong SN, so k = v+1 still holds - only a DISTINCTNESS check over the delivered set sees it. FIX: a per-node TX send lock across the synchronous push, taken in %push-data so every caller is covered without remembering; the ASYNC sender is deliberately NOT covered (it owns async-tx-msg and there is one of it). Lock order TX-OUTER / node-INNER, verified against flush-batch, announce-endpoints, stop-node, publish-relay-lifecycle and %dispose-or-unregister, none of which holds the node lock. MEASURED on Clasp where it failed most readily: 2 of 5 FAIL before (and 1 of 5 with the ADR 0108 window reverted, so it PRE-DATED that fix) -> 10 of 10 OK with the lock -> 4 of 6 FAIL again with the lock removed, the falsification catching a real duplicate at 48 distinct of 49 delivered. THE FALSIFICATION ALSO FOUND A DEFECT IN THE NEW ASSERTION: comparing distinct against WANT rather than GOT made it fire on a pure loss while naming duplication ('19 distinct of 19'), so each check now accuses exactly one mechanism - a diagnostic that names the wrong subsystem is worse than a silent failure. LEFT DELIBERATELY UNFIXED AND NAMED: (incf disc-node-batch-pending) is a per-node counter incremented unsynchronised by every application thread; a lost increment delays a flush by one sample, cannot corrupt a datagram, and the announce cadence bounds it.

THE PAL CONTRACT IS PORTED: 118 exports, 66 implementation-independent, 40 per-implementation, 4 of which landed with ADR 0111 slice 1 - the remaining 36 are done and VERIFIED GREEN with 0 failures. Most is a MIRROR of the Clasp PAL rather than an invention, because cffi, bordeaux-threads and static-vectors all load on AllegroCL and those are exactly what Clasp routes through. FIVE GENUINE DIVERGENCES, each PROBED on the real build and none inferred: (1) libatomic.so.1 must be loaded EXPLICITLY - __atomic_compare_exchange_8/_4 and __atomic_fetch_add_8 resolve to NIL in an Allegro image and to valid pointers after the load, where Clasp gets them free from its runtime; (2) excl::atomic-conditional-setf is (PLACE NEW OLD) - new BEFORE old, the reverse of our argument order - and returns T/NIL not the previous value, so a failure re-reads and that re-read is NOT atomic with the failed swap (sound only for a CAS retry loop, which is the only sanctioned use); (3) excl::incf-atomic returns the NEW value where SBCL's atomic-incf returns the OLD - opposite conventions, same contract; (4) excl::*restart-init-function* holds ONE function not a list, so hook registration CHAINS or a subsystem silently loses its foreign-pointer re-resolve after an image restart; (5) most-positive-fixnum is 2^60-1, NARROWER than SBCL's 2^62-1, so bit-packing sized against SBCL can become a bignum. Notes: ADR 0114, COMPLETING ADR 0113 section 5: :DDS-PAL NOW LOADS AND FUNCTIONS ON ALLEGROCL. pal-net.lisp was written against SB-BSD-SOCKETS, which SBCL and Clasp both bundle and AllegroCL does not. MEASUREMENT SHRANK THE SCOPE: of 68 functions, 32 are pure CFFI (mmap, POSIX+SysV shm, semaphores, pshared mutex/condvar) needing nothing, 20 need neither, and only 16 touch sb-bsd-sockets across 12 distinct symbols - and the HOT PATHS ALREADY BYPASS IT, calling sendto/recvfrom through CFFI and using sb-bsd-sockets only to obtain the integer file descriptor. A socket in this PAL is already an fd wrapper. DECISION: use AllegroCL's own socket: interface (93 exported symbols) rather than reimplement socket(2)/bind(2) through CFFI, which was the first plan and would have reinvented a maintained library. The mapping is 1:1 and the whole divergence is carried by TWO shims - %SOCKET-FD (socket-file-descriptor vs socket-os-fd) and %SOCKET-CLOSE (socket-close vs CLOSE, since an Allegro socket IS a stream). THE PROPERTY THAT HAD TO SURVIVE: socket-os-fd answers the same integer, so the raw CFFI sendto/recvfrom path - the reason NFR-MEM's per-datagram allocation is zero - works UNCHANGED; verified by round-tripping a datagram on loopback BEFORE any PAL code was written, so the port costs nothing on the hot path rather than trading it away. TWO DOCUMENTED SEMANTIC DIFFERENCES, NOT HIDDEN: (a) Allegro binds/listens AT CREATION via :local-host/:local-port/:backlog, so SO_REUSEPORT is applied AFTER the bind, unlike the sb-bsd-sockets path; (b) tcp-recv LOSES THE :TIMEOUT / :EOF DISTINCTION - sb-bsd-sockets reads n=NIL for SO_RCVTIMEO and n=0 for a clean close, while Allegro's stream read-sequence signals on timeout and this arm folds it into :EOF; the durability microservice retries either way so it is safe but COARSER, an NFR-PORT gap rather than an equivalence. Also (require :sock) is mandatory - the socket interface is a loadable module, not part of the base image. A BUG THIS INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED: routing every socket-file-descriptor call through %SOCKET-FD with a global replace also rewrote %SOCKET-FD's OWN BODY, turning its #-allegro arm into (%socket-fd socket) - unbounded recursion on SBCL and Clasp, the two implementations that were already green. Found by INSPECTION, not by the Allegro test, which takes the #+allegro branch and could never have exercised it: A PORT VERIFIED ONLY ON THE NEW PLATFORM CAN BREAK THE OLD ONES IN EXACTLY THE CODE THE PORT SHARES.

Method: Found by porting to a THIRD implementation; fixed; then verified on BOTH implementations of the CI host with a new arm driven from OCTETS rather than from a character, because constructing the character is exactly what the affected implementation cannot do
Artifact: src/dds-cdr/primitives.lisp (+replacement-character+, cdr-get-string); src/dds-tests/echo-test.lisp (run-utf8-supplementary-decode-test NEW, plus the encode and decode fixtures made representation-aware); docs/adr/0115-*.md
Notes: ADR 0115, A REMOTELY-TRIGGERABLE CRASH OF THE RECEIVE PATH. CDR-GET-STRING built its result with (setf (char s k) (code-char cp)). CODE-CHAR returns NIL for a code that is not a character in the implementation, and AllegroCL 11.0 has 16-BIT CHARACTERS - CHAR-CODE-LIMIT 65536, (code-char #x1F600) => NIL - so every SUPPLEMENTARY-PLANE scalar value (every emoji, all of CJK Extension B) made that SETF a TYPE ERROR SIGNALLED OUT OF THE RX PATH. THE INPUT IS NOT MALFORMED: F0 9F 98 80 is well-formed UTF-8 per RFC 3629 section 3 and exactly what a conformant peer sends for U+1F600, so any peer could crash an AllegroCL subscriber by publishing a string containing an emoji - a denial of service reachable from the network, violating NFR-SEC-POSTURE and the operating contract's no-conditions rule at once. SBCL (limit 1114112) and Clasp cannot reach it because CODE-CHAR never fails there for a valid scalar value: TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS AGREEING PROVES NOTHING ABOUT THE THIRD. FIX: substitute U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER, the Unicode-standard answer for this case and itself always representable (below the 16-bit limit). DELIBERATELY NOT SILENT - the application receives the replacement character and can see it, whereas dropping the sample discards data the peer legitimately sent and returning a status is ineffective because the generated codecs call CDR-GET-STRING in a single-value context and ignore it. It is a SUBSTITUTION, NOT A REJECTION: the existing :MALFORMED-UTF8 status stays reserved for genuinely ill-formed input (overlong, bare continuation, surrogate, beyond U+10FFFF) and must not be conflated. On SBCL and Clasp the OR arm is UNREACHABLE so their behaviour is byte-identical. NOT CLAIMED: AllegroCL still cannot REPRESENT a supplementary code point, so a round trip through an AllegroCL reader is lossy for that character - an implementation limit, now a VISIBLE SUBSTITUTION INSTEAD OF A CRASH, recorded as an NFR-PORT gap. THE SAME FIXTURE TRAP FOR THE THIRD TIME IN ONE DAY: both existing UTF-8 tests built their case as (string (code-char #x1F600)), which on AllegroCL is (string NIL) = the three-character string NIL, so they passed on SBCL while silently asserting the encoding of NIL where the bug lived - after the -0.0 literal (ADR 0111) and the drain-window sabotage that could not reach the code it sabotaged (ADR 0108). A FIXTURE THAT CANNOT CONSTRUCT ITS CASE DOES NOT FAIL, IT QUIETLY TESTS SOMETHING ELSE. Fixed three ways: the encode assertion is guarded and THE GUARD ITSELF IS ASSERTED (char-code-limit < #x1F600) so the skip cannot become a silent pass; the decode assertion expects the scalar value where representable and U+FFFD where not, still an OK-CASE because a substitution is not a rejection; and the new arm is driven FROM OCTETS. VERIFIED on both CI-host implementations: SBCL decodes U+1F600, AllegroCL decodes U+FFFD, neither signals.
